docs.title: TailoredApps .NET Shared Components
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation of TailoredApps Shared Components — a set of reusable .NET libraries that accelerate the development of professional web applications. Each library solves one specific problem and is designed for testability, extensibility, and integration with the ASP.NET Core + MediatR ecosystem.

docs.title: Upgrading from 1.x
docs.text:
Moving from 1.x to 2.0? The changes required in application code - handling a failing payment gateway, the required members of PaymentRequest, Tpay and Adyen webhooks - are collected on the Upgrading to 2.0 page.

The 3.0 line is in a test phase (3.0.0-preview.N): the MediatR libraries move to ForkForward.Mediator. What to change in an application: Upgrading to 3.0.

docs.title: Target frameworks
docs.text: From version 2.0 the libraries ship for net10.0 and net11.0; older frameworks are served by the 1.x packages (1.6.x). The net11.0 assets are compiled with runtime async. Details, limitations and how to switch it off: Target frameworks and runtime async.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install the chosen library
dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR
dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework
dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Payments

Full documentation for each library — including code examples, DI registration, and ready-made AI agent prompts — is available in the Libraries section in the side menu.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Before adding a new library, read the contributing guidelines and DOCUMENTATION_RULE.

Every new library must have a documentation page — PRs without one will be rejected.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to TailoredApps Shared Components! This document describes the contribution process and mandatory documentation requirements.

docs.title: General Rules
docs.text:
1. Fork → Feature Branch → PR — do not commit directly to master
  2. Branch naming: feature/<short-name> or fix/<short-name>
  3. One PR = one substantive change
  4. All tests must pass before opening a PR
  5. Code must have XML docs (summary) for public types and methods
  6. One namespace per file, declared without a block (namespace TailoredApps.Shared.Xxx;). .editorconfig enforces the style; fix existing code with dotnet format style TailoredApps.Shared.slnx --diagnostics IDE0161 --severity info

docs.title: Local Setup
docs.text:
.NET SDK 11.0.100 or newer is required — it builds both target frameworks (net10.0 and net11.0). The tests run on net10.0 and net11.0, so both runtimes are needed. The conventions for target frameworks and runtime async are described on the Target frameworks and runtime async page.

git clone https://github.com/tailored-apps/SharedComponents.git
cd SharedComponents

# .NET
export DOTNET_ROOT=/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet/libexec
export PATH="$PATH:/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet/bin"
dotnet restore

# Documentation
pip install mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve  # http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Solution and build output
docs.text:
The repository uses the XML solution format — TailoredApps.Shared.slnx (opened by the dotnet CLI and by Visual Studio 2022 17.13 or newer).

dotnet build TailoredApps.Shared.slnx
dotnet test TailoredApps.Shared.slnx

The root Directory.Build.props enables UseArtifactsOutput, so projects no longer create their own bin/ and obj/ folders. Everything goes to a single git-ignored artifacts/ directory:

Path Contents artifacts/bin/<Project>/<configuration>_<tfm>/ compiled libraries, e.g. artifacts/bin/TailoredApps.Shared.WebApi/release_net10.0/ artifacts/obj/<Project>/ intermediate files artifacts/package/<configuration>/ NuGet packages (*.nupkg) for every library — the release workflow publishes from here

To clean the build, delete the artifacts/ directory. Add a new library to the solution with dotnet sln TailoredApps.Shared.slnx add <path to .csproj> — the settings from Directory.Build.props apply automatically: target frameworks, language version, nullable, package metadata (author, MIT licence, project URL) and NuGet package generation. Package versions live in Directory.Packages.props, and nuget.config limits the sources to nuget.org. *.user files and the .vs/, .idea/, .vscode/ folders are never committed (they are in .gitignore).

docs.title: 🔴 IRON RULE OF DOCUMENTATION
docs.text:
Every new library in this repo MUST have a documentation page in docs/Libraries/.

PR without documentation = PR rejected.

docs.title: Requirements for each documentation page
docs.text:
Each docs/Libraries/<LibraryName>/index.md page must contain:

  1. Header + badges — library name, NuGet and license badges
  2. Description — in Polish 🇵🇱 and in English 🇬🇧
  3. Installation — dotnet add package ...
  4. DI Registration — example with Program.cs
  5. Usage example — real, complete C# code (not a toy example)
  6. API Reference — table/list of main interfaces and classes
  7. 🤖 AI Agent Prompt — ready-made prompt to paste into an AI agent context

docs.title: Navigation update
docs.text: After adding a library page, update the nav: section in mkdocs.yml and the library table on docs/index.md.

docs.title: Both languages and the package README
docs.text:
• The site has two trees: docs/ (Polish) and docs-en/ (English). Every page exists in both, with the same relative path, and is registered in both mkdocs.yml and mkdocs-en.yml; the library table is on both docs/index.md and docs-en/index.md. A change to a library updates both.
  • Every library has a README.md next to its csproj: what the package is, installation, registration, a usage example, configuration, and a link to its page on this site. It is packed into the NuGet package automatically (src/Directory.Build.props) and is what nuget.org shows - nothing has to be added to the csproj.
  • Code samples must compile against the current source: check type, method and configuration key names in the code, not from memory.

docs.title: The demo application and the integration tests
docs.text: The demo application (samples/TailoredApps.Shared.Demo) uses every library, and tests/TailoredApps.Shared.IntegrationTests drives it over HTTP. A new library is added to the demo too, with a test of its scenario; a change after which a library is used differently updates the demo. The demo runs without a network: an external service is replaced at the transport level (an HTTP handler), never by changing the library.

docs.title: Pre-PR Checklist
docs.text:
• Code compiles without errors (dotnet build)
  • Tests pass (dotnet test)
  • XML docs added to public types
  • Documentation page in docs/Libraries/
  • mkdocs.yml nav updated
  • Table on docs/index.md updated
  • mkdocs build --strict passes without errors
  • dotnet build TailoredApps.Shared.slnx -c Release -p:ValidatePublicApi=true passes (no change incompatible with 2.0.0)

docs.title: Public API compatibility
docs.text:
The master branch is the 3.0 line in a test phase (3.0.0-preview.N): breaking changes are allowed until 3.0.0, but only on purpose. The release/2.1 branch is the 2.1.x fix line, compatible with 2.0.0. On master the TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR* libraries are left out of the comparison (they moved from MediatR to ForkForward.Mediator); the others are still compared, so that a breaking change does not happen by accident.

The 2.x line must stay compatible with 2.0.0: code compiled against any 2.x version has to work with every later 2.x. The Build & Test PR check compares the public API of every library with its 2.0.0 package on nuget.org and fails on a breaking change (removing a public type or member, or changing its signature - CP0001, CP0002, …). Adding API is allowed.

# the same locally
dotnet build TailoredApps.Shared.slnx -c Release -p:ValidatePublicApi=true
  • The baseline version is set by PublicApiBaselineVersion in src/Directory.Build.targets.
  • A new library: until its first release add <SkipPublicApiValidation>true</SkipPublicApiValidation> to its csproj, and after the release replace it with <PublicApiBaselineVersion> holding the first version it was published in.
  • On the 2.x line, instead of removing a member, mark it [Obsolete] and add a new one; the removal waits for a major version.
  • A deliberate removal on the 3.0 line is recorded in the library's CompatibilitySuppressions.xml - member by member, so the rest of its API stays guarded. dotnet build src/<Library>/<Library>.csproj -c Release -p:ValidatePublicApi=true -p:ApiCompatGenerateSuppressionFile=true generates the file; review it before committing - it must hold only what you remove on purpose.

docs.title: Releasing (maintainers)
docs.text:
Pushing a tag vX.Y.Z (or a pre-release such as v2.0.0-preview.1) runs the Create Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml): it builds every library with the version taken from the tag, runs the tests, and publishes the packages from artifacts/package/release to nuget.org. The job fails if any package could not be published. Release notes creates the GitHub Release from the merged pull requests.

Packages are published through nuget.org Trusted Publishing — the repository stores no NuGet API key. The job requests a GitHub OIDC token and nuget.org exchanges it for an API key that is valid for one hour. This needs a one-time setup:

Where Setting nuget.org → account menu → Trusted Publishing → new policy Repository Owner tailored-apps, Repository SharedComponents, Workflow File release.yml (file name only), Environment nuget GitHub → repository settings → Secrets and variables → Actions Secret NUGET_USER: the nuget.org profile name (not the e-mail address) of the account that owns the policy GitHub → repository settings → Environments Environment nuget; add required reviewers to make every release wait for approval

The policy covers every package owned by the account or organisation chosen as its owner. The same workflow file serves the release/* maintenance branches, so one policy is enough for all release lines.

docs.title: Demo application and integration tests
docs.text:
3.0 line (test phase)

The demo is in the repository from the 3.0 line (master) and uses the MediatR libraries on ForkForward.Mediator (see Upgrading to 3.0). It is not a NuGet package and is never published to nuget.org.

samples/TailoredApps.Shared.Demo is a small shop built as an ASP.NET Core Web API that uses all 26 libraries together: a product catalogue, orders, payments through nine gateways, gateway notifications and a confirmation e-mail. It runs with no account and no network: the payment gateways are faked, e-mail goes to the console, and the database is SQLite in memory.

tests/TailoredApps.Shared.IntegrationTests starts the application in memory (WebApplicationFactory) and drives it over HTTP. CI runs these tests with the rest of the solution, so a library change that breaks how the libraries work together stops the PR.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
dotnet run --project samples/TailoredApps.Shared.Demo -f net10.0

The http profile in Properties/launchSettings.json listens on http://localhost:5080 in the Development environment. For net11.0 the demo is compiled with runtime async, as the libraries are (Target frameworks).

The integration tests:

dotnet test tests/TailoredApps.Shared.IntegrationTests/TailoredApps.Shared.IntegrationTests.csproj -f net10.0

docs.title: A walk through the shop
docs.text:
Every command works in Git Bash and in a Linux or macOS shell (openssl computes the notification signature).

# Products: page 1, the three most expensive
curl "http://localhost:5080/api/products?count=3&sortField=Price&sortDir=Desc"

# An order: green tea and a teapot
curl -X POST http://localhost:5080/api/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customerEmail":"anna@demo.example","productIds":[1,6]}'
# {"number":"ORD-20261112-cbef5f49","amount":153.9,"status":"New",...}

# A Revolut payment: the address of the payment page and the payment id
curl -X POST http://localhost:5080/api/orders/ORD-20261112-cbef5f49/checkout -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider":"Revolut","channel":"card"}'
# {"number":"ORD-20261112-cbef5f49","paymentId":"REVOLUT-1","redirectUrl":"https://gateway.demo/pay/revolut/REVOLUT-1"}

# The payment notification, signed the way Revolut signs it (the secret from appsettings.json)
body='{"event":"ORDER_COMPLETED","order_id":"REVOLUT-1"}'
ts=$(( $(date +%s) * 1000 ))
sig=$(printf 'v1.%s.%s' "$ts" "$body" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac 'demo-not-a-real-secret' | sed 's/^.*= //')
curl -X POST http://localhost:5080/api/webhooks/Revolut -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Revolut-Request-Timestamp: $ts" -H "Revolut-Signature: v1=$sig" -d "$body"
# OK - and on the application console: recipent: anna@demo.example; topic: Order ORD-20261112-cbef5f49 is paid; ...

curl http://localhost:5080/api/orders/ORD-20261112-cbef5f49
# "status":"Paid","paidAt":"..."

The notification timestamp has to be current: Revolut rejects signatures older than 300 seconds (WebhookToleranceSeconds).

docs.title: What is faked
docs.text:
• Payment gateways - Payments/FakeGateway.cs is the primary handler of the providers' named HTTP clients (AddHttpClient(name).ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(...)) and answers the way each gateway does. The first path segment names the gateway: the ServiceUrl values in appsettings.json point to https://gateway.demo/<gateway>. Stripe works through its own SDK, so the demo registers an IStripeClient that uses the same handler. The provider libraries run unchanged - only the transport is replaced.
  • Gateway outage and refusal - FakeGatewayState.Unavailable makes every gateway answer 503, and FakeGatewayState.Refusing 400; the tests check that checkout then answers 503 or 422 and the order stays as it was.
  • Real gateways - set Demo:UseFakeGateways to false and put sandbox credentials in the configuration (user secrets preferably).
  • Notification signatures are verified for real, with the placeholder keys of appsettings.json.
  • E-mail - the console provider of the Email library; the tests replace it with a provider that records the messages.
  • Database - SQLite in memory on one open connection, seeded at start. SQLite has no decimal type, so amounts are stored in minor units and times in UTC ticks - exact, and sortable in SQL.

docs.title: The integration tests
docs.text:
Class What it checks WebApiDefaultsTests /health and /alive CatalogTests paging, sorting, the filter, parameter validation (400 naming the field; one Information entry without field values in the log, no Error), the cache (a second read does not run the handler), 404, retry and fallback OrdersTests saving and committing through the filter, rollback after 400, 404, checkout at all 9 gateways (with the HTTP request to the gateway), a gateway outage (503) and a refusal (422) - Stripe included - with the order unchanged WebhookTests a signed notification → the order is paid and one e-mail is sent from the template (also when the notification is repeated), a declined payment, a wrong signature and an old timestamp → 400 MinimalApiTests the minimal-API endpoints: a commit without SaveChanges, 400 with the validator's fields, a rollback after 409, 404 from the provider ApplicationTests the providers and channels, 501 for ML and Office365 when they are not configured

The tests change two things in the application: the clock (TimeProvider, frozen at a fixed instant) and the e-mail provider. Everything else is the application's own configuration. Code coverage from these tests counts for the libraries; the demo assembly is excluded.

docs.title: Lessons for your own application
docs.text:
• Actions do not call SaveChanges: the transaction filter saves and commits after a successful action and rolls back after a 4xx/5xx result or an exception.
  • Checkout catches HttpRequestException (including PaymentGatewayException) and answers 503 - the payment may or may not exist. That one block covers all nine providers, Stripe included; the demo turns a gateway refusal (Rejected) into 422.
  • Gateway notifications go to one endpoint with the raw body; the answer is the provider's ResponseObject (Tpay: TRUE, Adyen: [accepted]). A repeated notification changes nothing.
  • PaymentRequest.AdditionalData carries the application's own order number - Tpay and Adyen identify the payment by it in the notification.
  • A validator checks the paging and sorting parameters (400 naming the field), and the request has a default page and sort order, because without them the query extensions return the whole table in no particular order.
  • Values shown to the customer (the amount in the e-mail) are formatted independently of the server's culture.

docs.title: 🤖 AI Agent Prompt
docs.text:
Use the TailoredApps demo (samples/TailoredApps.Shared.Demo in the SharedComponents repository) as the reference for wiring
TailoredApps.Shared.* libraries into an ASP.NET Core Web API.

Registration (Program.cs, in this order):
- builder.AddTailoredWebApiDefaults(); builder.Services.AddDateTimeProvider();
- builder.Services.AddExceptionHandlingForWebApi<IExceptionHandlingProvider, MyExceptionHandlingProvider>();
- builder.Services.AddDbContext<MyDbContext>(...); builder.Services.AddUnitOfWorkForWebApi<IMyDbContext, MyDbContext>();
- builder.Services.AddControllers(o => { o.Filters.AddUnitOfWorkTransactionAttribute(); o.Filters.AddExceptionHandlingFilterAttribute(); });
- builder.Services.AddMediator(cfg => cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly));
  var pipeline = new PipelineRegistration(builder.Services); pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors(); pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors(typeof(Program).Assembly);
- validators: builder.Services.AddTransient<IValidator<TRequest>, TRequestValidator>();
- builder.Services.AddPayments().RegisterRevolutProvider()...; e-mail: RegisterConsoleProvider() or the SMTP provider, plus IMailMessageBuilder.
- app.ConfigureExceptionHandler(); app.MapTailoredWebApiDefaults(); app.MapControllers();

What gets configured: health endpoints, OpenTelemetry, HTTP client resilience; one TimeProvider clock; JSON error responses;
a unit of work committed or rolled back per request; the MediatR pipeline (logging, validation, caching, fallback, retry);
payment providers behind IPaymentService; template e-mail.

Configuration: WebApiDefaults, Payments:Providers:<Provider>, Mail:Providers:<Provider>; the demo's appsettings.json lists every key.

Rules:
- Never call SaveChanges in a controller action; return a 4xx result to roll the request back.
- Wrap RegisterPayment and GetStatus in catch (HttpRequestException) and answer 503 (every provider, Stripe included); answer
  PaymentStatus == Rejected with 422.
- Pass the raw request body to HandleWebhookAsync and answer with PaymentResponse.ResponseObject; make the handling idempotent.
- Put the application's own order number in PaymentRequest.AdditionalData.
- Validate paging and sorting parameters with FluentValidation and give paged requests a default page and sort order.
- Use `using ForkForward.Mediator;` and AddMediator (3.0 line), never the MediatR package.

docs.title: How the automated bump works
docs.text:
The workflow runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC (and on demand via workflow dispatch). It executes scripts/Bump-Deps.ps1, which takes every package in Directory.Packages.props (the central PackageVersion items) and queries nuget.org for its latest stable version. Entries from before version 2.0 name individual *.csproj files, because each project then carried its own versions.

Rule Behaviour Wildcard versions (10.*, 2.*) left alone — they self-update on restore Pre-release versions ignored Latest version's license outside the allowlist (MIT, Apache-2.0) SKIP License differs between the pinned and the latest version SKIP (relicensing guard) No declared SPDX license SKIP (unless -AllowUndeclaredLicense) Package on the -Ignore list (e.g. MediatR >= 13.0.0, RPL-1.5) clamped to the highest version below the ceiling

After bumping, the workflow builds the whole solution (dotnet build), generates the entry on this page, and only then opens a PR labelled dependencies and automated.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Calling DateTime.Now directly in production code makes deterministic tests impossible. The library provides IDateTimeProvider - the current date and time as ready-to-use values (DateTime, DateTimeOffset, TimeSpan), read from a clock that can be replaced in tests.

Since 2.0 that clock is System.TimeProvider from .NET: DateTimeProvider reads every value from it. An application therefore has one clock - code that injects IDateTimeProvider and code that injects TimeProvider (timers, delays, .NET libraries) see the same time and the same time zone, in tests with FakeTimeProvider as well.

Which one to use:

You need Inject The current date or time as a value (UtcNow, OffsetUtcNow, Today, …) IDateTimeProvider A timer, a delay, a time measurement (CreateTimer, Task.Delay(…, timeProvider), GetTimestamp) TimeProvider

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.DateTime

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.DateTime;

builder.Services.AddDateTimeProvider();

AddDateTimeProvider() registers, as singletons, TimeProvider (TimeProvider.System) and an IDateTimeProvider that reads it. Registrations already in the container are kept - your own TimeProvider can be registered before or after the call, and IDateTimeProvider always reads the one the container resolves.

docs.title: Production code
docs.text:
public class OrderService
{
    private readonly IDateTimeProvider _dateTime;

    public OrderService(IDateTimeProvider dateTime) => _dateTime = dateTime;

    public Order CreateOrder(string customerId, decimal amount)
    {
        var now = _dateTime.OffsetUtcNow;   // DateTimeOffset: the instant together with its offset from UTC
        return new Order
        {
            Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
            CustomerId = customerId,
            Amount = amount,
            CreatedAt = now,
            ExpiresAt = now.AddDays(30),
        };
    }

    public bool IsOrderExpired(Order order) => order.ExpiresAt < _dateTime.OffsetUtcNow;
}

docs.title: Unit test (FakeTimeProvider)
docs.text:
dotnet add package Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing

using Microsoft.Extensions.Time.Testing;
using TailoredApps.Shared.DateTime;
using Xunit;

public class OrderServiceTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void When_Thirty_Days_Pass_Should_Report_The_Order_As_Expired()
    {
        // Arrange
        var clock = new FakeTimeProvider(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 6, 1, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
        var service = new OrderService(new DateTimeProvider(clock));
        var order = service.CreateOrder("customer-1", 99.99m);

        // Act
        clock.Advance(TimeSpan.FromDays(31));

        // Assert
        Assert.True(service.IsOrderExpired(order));
    }
}

A mock of the interface (new Mock<IDateTimeProvider>()) works as before; FakeTimeProvider has the advantage that time can be advanced and every property stays consistent with the others.

docs.title: Integration test - replacing the clock in the host
docs.text:
var clock = new FakeTimeProvider(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 6, 1, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));

await using var factory = new WebApplicationFactory<Program>().WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>
    builder.ConfigureServices(services => services.AddSingleton<TimeProvider>(clock)));
// IDateTimeProvider and TimeProvider in the application now both point at "clock"

docs.title: DateTime or DateTimeOffset
docs.text:
• For values that are stored in a database or sent on, use OffsetUtcNow (or OffsetNow): a DateTimeOffset carries the offset from UTC, which a DateTime does not - its Kind is lost in serialization and in most databases.
  • Now and Today report the time zone of the clock (TimeProvider.LocalTimeZone), with Kind == Local.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Type Kind Description IDateTimeProvider Interface The current date and time as ready-to-use values DateTimeProvider Class Implementation on TimeProvider: new DateTimeProvider() reads the system clock, new DateTimeProvider(timeProvider) the given one DateTimeProviderExtensions.AddDateTimeProvider() Extension method Registers TimeProvider and IDateTimeProvider as singletons (without replacing existing ones) IDateTimeProvider.OffsetUtcNow Property The current instant in UTC as a DateTimeOffset (zero offset) IDateTimeProvider.OffsetNow Property The current instant in the local time zone of the clock as a DateTimeOffset, with that zone's offset IDateTimeProvider.UtcNow Property Current UTC time as a DateTime (Kind == Utc) IDateTimeProvider.Now Property Current time in the local time zone of the clock as a DateTime (Kind == Local) IDateTimeProvider.UtcToday Property Current UTC date IDateTimeProvider.Today Property Current date in the local time zone of the clock IDateTimeProvider.UtcTimeOfDay Property Time of day in UTC as a TimeSpan IDateTimeProvider.TimeOfDay Property Time of day (local) as a TimeSpan DateTimeProvider.TimeProvider Property The clock every value is read from

Compatibility with 1.x: OffsetNow, OffsetUtcNow and UtcTimeOfDay have default implementations in the interface, so your own implementations of IDateTimeProvider and existing mocks compile unchanged. Behaviour change: Now and Today report the time zone of the TimeProvider in use rather than always the system zone (the same thing for the system clock).

## TailoredApps.Shared.DateTime - instructions for an AI agent

You are using TailoredApps.Shared.DateTime: IDateTimeProvider is the current date and time read from System.TimeProvider.

### Registration
// Program.cs
builder.Services.AddDateTimeProvider();

### What gets configured
- TimeProvider (TimeProvider.System) - the only clock of the application, singleton
- IDateTimeProvider (DateTimeProvider) - date and time values read from that clock, singleton
- Existing registrations of TimeProvider and IDateTimeProvider are not replaced

### Configuration
- No configuration keys. Another clock: services.AddSingleton<TimeProvider>(myClock) before or after AddDateTimeProvider()

### Rules
- Do not call DateTime.Now, DateTime.UtcNow or DateTimeOffset.UtcNow directly in production code
- Inject IDateTimeProvider when a date or time value is needed; TimeProvider when a timer, a delay or a time measurement is needed
- For values stored in a database or sent on use OffsetUtcNow (DateTimeOffset), not UtcNow (DateTime)
- Now / Today / OffsetNow only where local time is needed (for display, for example)
- Use UtcTimeOfDay; the misspelled UtcTimeOfDaty was removed in 3.0
- In tests: new DateTimeProvider(new FakeTimeProvider(...)) from the Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing package; move time with Advance
- Do not register a second, independent clock next to TimeProvider - the application must have one source of time

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This library provides a complete abstraction for sending email messages in .NET applications. It is built around the IEmailProvider interface, which can be swapped depending on the environment — in production use SmtpEmailProvider (sends via SMTP), in local development use EmailServiceToConsolleWritter (prints to console without actual delivery).

The library also includes a template-based email body building system (IMailMessageBuilder), supporting simple token substitution (DefaultMessageBuilder) or file-system templates with {{token}} placeholders (TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilder).

Built-in safeguard against accidental spam in non-production environments: when IsProd = false, all emails are redirected to the CatchAll address instead of real recipients.

docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Email

{
  "Mail": {
    "Providers": {
      "Smtp": {
        "Host": "smtp.example.com",
        "Port": 587,
        "UserName": "noreply@example.com",
        "Password": "secret",
        "From": "noreply@example.com",
        "EnableSsl": true,
        "IsProd": true,
        "CatchAll": "dev@example.com"

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
public class NotificationService
{
    private readonly IEmailProvider _emailProvider;
    private readonly IMailMessageBuilder _messageBuilder;

    public NotificationService(
        IEmailProvider emailProvider,
        IMailMessageBuilder messageBuilder)
    {
        _emailProvider = emailProvider;
        _messageBuilder = messageBuilder;
    }

    public async Task SendWelcomeEmailAsync(string recipientEmail, string userName)
    {
        var body = _messageBuilder.Build(
            templateKey: "welcome.html",
            variables: new Dictionary<string, string>
            {
                { "UserName", userName },
                { "AppUrl", "https://myapp.example.com" }
            },
            templates: null  // loaded from disk when Location is configured
        );

        var messageId = await _emailProvider.SendMail(
            recipnet: recipientEmail,
            topic: "Welcome to MyApp!",
            messageBody: body,
            attachments: null
        );

        Console.WriteLine($"Email sent, MessageId: {messageId}");
    }

    public async Task SendInvoiceAsync(
        string recipientEmail,
        string subject,
        string htmlBody,
        byte[] pdfBytes)
    {
        await _emailProvider.SendMail(
            recipnet: recipientEmail,
            topic: subject,
            messageBody: htmlBody,
            attachments: new Dictionary<string, byte[]>
            {
                { "invoice.pdf", pdfBytes }
            }
        );
    }
}

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Type Kind Description IEmailProvider Interface Main contract: SendMail, GetMail SmtpEmailProvider Class Sends via SMTP; options from SmtpEmailServiceOptions. GetMail is not implemented (NotImplementedException) EmailServiceToConsolleWritter Class Writes the email data to the console (dev/test); GetMail returns an empty list. The class name is spelled this way in the API SmtpEmailServiceOptions Class SMTP configuration: Host, Port, UserName, Password, From, EnableSsl, IsProd, CatchAll IMailMessageBuilder Interface Contract: Build(templateKey, variables, templates) DefaultMessageBuilder Class Substitutes tokens in the template dictionary TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilder Class Loads templates from the file system; {{token}} placeholders TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilderOptions Class Location (template directory path), FileExtension SmtpEmailProviderExtensions.RegisterSmtpProvider Ext. method Registers SmtpEmailProvider in DI SmtpEmailProviderExtensions.RegisterConsoleProvider Ext. method Registers EmailServiceToConsolleWritter in DI

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• Template variables are HTML-encoded. Message bodies are sent as HTML and {{token}} values often come from users (display names, free text). TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilder and DefaultMessageBuilder encode values (WebUtility.HtmlEncode), so <a href="https://evil"> cannot become a phishing link in a message from a trusted sender. Insert values that intentionally contain HTML with triple braces {{{token}}}; turn encoding off globally with TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilderOptions.HtmlEncodeVariables = false or new DefaultMessageBuilder(htmlEncodeVariables: false).
  • Single-pass replacement. A value containing {{OtherToken}} is never expanded again.
  • Exactly one recipient. SmtpEmailProvider.SendMail accepts one address; a comma- or semicolon-separated list throws FormatException (previously MailAddressCollection.Add silently added extra recipients).
  • TLS on by default. Mail:Providers:Smtp:EnableSsl now defaults to true.
  • CatchAll is required outside production. With IsProd = false a missing CatchAll throws InvalidOperationException instead of sending nowhere.

docs.text: A lightweight package containing only the MailMessage data model — a representation of an email message. Separating the model into its own package allows other libraries (e.g. TailoredApps.Shared.Email.Office365) to depend only on the model without pulling in the full SMTP implementation.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
using TailoredApps.Shared.Email.Models;

// Example: listing the received messages
ICollection<MailMessage> messages = await emailProvider.GetMail(
    folder: "Inbox",
    sender: "boss@company.com",
    fromLast: TimeSpan.FromDays(7)
);

foreach (var msg in messages)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[{msg.Date:yyyy-MM-dd}] From: {msg.Sender}");
    Console.WriteLine($"  Subject: {msg.Topic}");
    Console.WriteLine($"  To:      {msg.Recipent}");

    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(msg.HtmlBody))
        Console.WriteLine($"  (HTML body, {msg.HtmlBody.Length} characters)");

    if (msg.Attachements?.Count > 0)
        Console.WriteLine($"  Attachments: {string.Join(", ", msg.Attachements.Keys)}");
}

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
An IEmailProvider implementation that reads email from Microsoft 365 using IMAP with OAuth2 authentication (client credentials flow). The library authenticates with Azure AD as a confidential client application — supporting both client secret and certificate authentication.

This allows you to receive messages from an Office 365 mailbox without storing a user password. The library automatically handles token acquisition and caching via Microsoft Identity.

SendMail — not implemented

The SendMail method throws NotImplementedException. This library supports reading only via IMAP. For sending, use SmtpEmailProvider or Microsoft Graph integration.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Email.Office365

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.Email.Office365;

builder.Services.RegisterOffice365Provider();

docs.title: appsettings.json configuration
docs.text:
{
  "Mail": {
    "Providers": {
      "Office365": {
        "Instance": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{0}",
        "Tenant": "your-tenant-id-or-domain.onmicrosoft.com",
        "ClientId": "your-application-client-id",
        "MailBox": "shared-mailbox@yourdomain.com",
        "ClientSecret": "your-client-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}

Instance is optional - the value above is its default. AuthenticationConfig also binds ApiUrl (default https://graph.microsoft.com/), but the provider does not use it: it always connects over IMAP to outlook.office365.com:993 and requests a token for https://outlook.office365.com/.default.

docs.title: Azure AD configuration
docs.text:
The application in Azure AD needs application permissions (not delegated ones):

  • IMAP.AccessAsApp — IMAP access as an application
  • Administration: New-ServicePrincipalAllowedToUseApp for the specific mailbox

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
public class MailboxMonitorService
{
    private readonly IEmailProvider _emailProvider;

    public MailboxMonitorService(IEmailProvider emailProvider)
    {
        _emailProvider = emailProvider;
    }

    public async Task<ICollection<MailMessage>> GetNewOrdersAsync()
    {
        // Get the messages from the last 24 hours from a specific sender
        var messages = await _emailProvider.GetMail(
            folder: "Orders",                     // a sub-folder of the Inbox (Inbox/Orders)
            sender: "orders@partner.com",
            fromLast: TimeSpan.FromHours(24)
        );

        return messages;
    }

    public async Task<ICollection<MailMessage>> GetAllFromInboxAsync()
    {
        // Get all messages from the inbox (read and unread)
        return await _emailProvider.GetMail();
    }
}

folder names a sub-folder of the Inbox; an empty value (the default) means the Inbox itself, so folder: "Inbox" would look for Inbox/Inbox. The folder is opened read-only. sender and recipent are "contains" filters and fromLast limits the result to messages delivered after now minus that time span; without filters every message in the folder is downloaded.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This library provides a complete implementation of the Unit of Work pattern on top of Entity Framework Core. It solves the problem of uncontrolled transaction management in multi-layer applications — instead of calling SaveChanges() directly in each repository, you have a single control point (IUnitOfWork) managing the transaction lifecycle.

Key capabilities: - Transactions with configurable isolation levels - Auditing — automatic collection of entity changes (which entity, its state, original and current values), handed to your IEntityChangesAuditor when the transaction is committed - Hooks — IHook implementations that execute code before/after SaveChanges or after a transaction commit/rollback - InMemory provider support for testing

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.Interfaces.Audit;
using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.UnitOfWork;
using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.Audit.Configuration;

// The DbContext itself is registered the usual way (AddDbContext<ApplicationDbContext>(...))

// Basic registration
builder.Services.AddUnitOfWork<IApplicationDbContext, ApplicationDbContext>();

// ...or with hooks and auditing (see the examples below)
builder.Services.AddUnitOfWork<IApplicationDbContext, ApplicationDbContext>()
    .WithPostSaveChangesHook<SaveLoggingHook>()
    .WithUnitOfWorkAudit<ApplicationDbContext, AuditLogAuditor>(settings =>
    {
        settings.TypesToCollect = new[] { typeof(Order), typeof(Customer) };
        settings.EntityStatesToCollect = new[]
        {
            AuditEntityState.Added,
            AuditEntityState.Modified,
            AuditEntityState.Deleted
        };
    });

Where IApplicationDbContext is the interface of your DbContext and ApplicationDbContext is the implementation inheriting from DbContext. AddUnitOfWork resolves ApplicationDbContext from the container, so it has to be registered. WithUnitOfWorkAudit requires at least one entry in both TypesToCollect and EntityStatesToCollect; an empty list throws InvalidAuditConfigurationException.

docs.text:
public interface IApplicationDbContext
{
    DbSet<Order> Orders { get; }
    DbSet<Customer> Customers { get; }
    DbSet<Account> Accounts { get; }
}

public class ApplicationDbContext : DbContext, IApplicationDbContext
{
    public DbSet<Order> Orders { get; set; }
    public DbSet<Customer> Customers { get; set; }
    public DbSet<Account> Accounts { get; set; }

    public ApplicationDbContext(DbContextOptions<ApplicationDbContext> options)
        : base(options) { }
}

docs.title: Usage in a service
docs.text:
public class OrderService
{
    private readonly IUnitOfWork<IApplicationDbContext> _uow;

    public OrderService(IUnitOfWork<IApplicationDbContext> uow)
    {
        _uow = uow;
    }

    public async Task<Order> CreateOrderAsync(CreateOrderRequest request)
    {
        var order = new Order
        {
            CustomerId = request.CustomerId,
            TotalAmount = request.TotalAmount,
            Status = OrderStatus.Pending
        };

        _uow.DataProvider.Orders.Add(order);
        await _uow.SaveChangesAsync();

        return order;
    }

    public async Task TransferFundsAsync(int fromId, int toId, decimal amount)
    {
        // Manual transaction control with an isolation level
        _uow.SetIsolationLevel(System.Data.IsolationLevel.Serializable);

        // Without this call the transaction would open only on the first SaveChanges,
        // and the reads below would run outside it
        _uow.BeginTransactionManually();

        try
        {
            var from = await _uow.DataProvider.Accounts.FindAsync(fromId);
            var to = await _uow.DataProvider.Accounts.FindAsync(toId);

            from.Balance -= amount;
            to.Balance += amount;

            await _uow.SaveChangesAsync();
            _uow.CommitTransaction();
        }
        catch
        {
            _uow.RollbackTransaction();
            throw;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Hook — example of logging after a save
docs.text:
A hook implements one of the four hook interfaces - IPreSaveChangesHook, IPostSaveChangesHook, ITransactionCommitHook, ITransactionRollbackHook - which all derive from IHook and have a single method, Execute(), without parameters. Register it with the matching With...Hook<T>() method on the builder returned by AddUnitOfWork.

using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.Interfaces.UnitOfWork;

// Runs after every SaveChanges / SaveChangesAsync of the unit of work
public class SaveLoggingHook : IPostSaveChangesHook
{

docs.text:
A hook does not receive the changed entities. They are collected by the audit extension (WithUnitOfWorkAudit) and passed to your IEntityChangesAuditor after the transaction is committed; a rollback discards them.

using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.Interfaces.Audit;

public class AuditLogAuditor : IEntityChangesAuditor
{
    private readonly ILogger<AuditLogAuditor> _logger;

    public AuditLogAuditor(ILogger<AuditLogAuditor> logger) => _logger = logger;

    public void AuditChanges(IEnumerable<EntityChange> entityChanges)
    {
        foreach (var change in entityChanges)
            _logger.LogInformation("Entity {Type}: {State}",
                change.EntityType?.Name, change.State);
    }
}

docs.title: 🔒 Query security
docs.text:
• Page size is bounded. PagingQuery<T> rejects (ArgumentOutOfRangeException) Page < 1, Count < 1, Count > PagingQuery<T>.MaxPageSize (default 1000, settable globally or per constructor) and Skip overflow. A ?count=2147483647 request no longer materialises the whole table.

The ApplySorting(sorting, allowedSortFields) overload restricts sorting to an explicit list of properties - use it for entities with sensitive columns.
var page = await db.Users
    .ApplySorting(request, allowedSortFields: new[] { "Name", "CreatedDateUtc" })
    .PagingAsync(request);

PagingAsync

Up to 2.0.0-preview PagingAsync failed with InvalidOperationException ("The source 'IQueryable' doesn't implement 'IAsyncEnumerable'") for every non-empty page, because it materialised the PagingQuery<T> wrapper instead of the EF Core query. Fixed: the page is read from PagingQuery<T>.Query. Use the same property when you call ToListAsync on a PagingQuery<T> yourself.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A transaction per request for minimal APIs: an endpoint filter that ends an endpoint with a commit or a rollback of the unit of work of TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework. It is the counterpart of the MVC filter in UnitOfWork.WebApiCore - with the same rules - for applications without controllers. The library is a package of its own; it changes nothing in the existing ones.

  • Commits after the endpoint succeeds (pending changes are saved first) - the endpoint does not call SaveChanges
  • Rolls back after an exception, or when the endpoint returned a result with a status of 400 or more (Results.BadRequest(), Results.Conflict(), …)
  • An endpoint that returns a plain object, or a result without a status code, counts as a success
  • Optionally sets the isolation level for an endpoint or a group

NativeAOT

The filter itself uses no reflection, but the library depends on Entity Framework Core, which is not ready for NativeAOT (see Trimming and NativeAOT). Minimal APIs without AOT work without restrictions.

docs.title: Installation

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.MinimalApi;

builder.Services.AddDbContext<ShopDbContext>(options => options.UseSqlServer(connectionString));
builder.Services.AddUnitOfWorkForMinimalApi<IShopDbContext, ShopDbContext>();

AddUnitOfWorkForMinimalApi registers what AddUnitOfWork of TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework does and returns the same builder (hooks, auditing). An application that already calls AddUnitOfWorkForWebApi for its controllers does not register the unit of work twice.

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.Interfaces.UnitOfWork;
using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.MinimalApi;

// A whole group in a transaction
var products = app.MapGroup("/api/products").WithUnitOfWorkTransaction();

products.MapPost("/", async (NewProduct product, IUnitOfWork<IShopDbContext> unitOfWork, CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
{
    var db = unitOfWork.DataProvider;
    db.Products.Add(new Product { Name = product.Name, Price = product.Price });

    // The product is already in the context. Answering 409 makes the filter roll it back.
    if (await db.Products.AnyAsync(p => p.Name == product.Name, cancellationToken))
        return Results.Conflict();

    return Results.Created($"/api/products/{product.Name}", product);   // commit - no SaveChanges
});

// One endpoint with its own isolation level
app.MapPost("/api/transfers", (Transfer transfer, IUnitOfWork<IShopDbContext> unitOfWork) => { /* ... */ })
   .WithUnitOfWorkTransaction(IsolationLevel.Serializable);

Filters run in the order they are added. With ExceptionHandling.MinimalApi add exception handling first, so that it also answers for an exception thrown by the commit:

app.MapGroup("/api/products")
   .WithExceptionHandling()          // outer: turns an exception into the error response
   .WithUnitOfWorkTransaction();     // inner: commit / rollback

docs.title: 🔒 Transaction consistency
docs.text:
• Rollback on an error response, not only on an exception: partial writes made before return Results.Conflict() do not stay in the database.
  • A failed commit is not lost. When the commit fails the transaction is rolled back and the commit exception is thrown; when the rollback fails too, both end up in an AggregateException.
  • The transaction opens lazily - at the first SaveChanges / SaveChangesAsync (the commit at the end counts) or after BeginTransactionManually(). Call BeginTransactionManually() before a read that has to be protected by the transaction.
  • Isolation levels: ReadCommitted by default; ReadCommitted, ReadUncommitted and Serializable are supported.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
ASP.NET Core Web API integration for Unit of Work — eliminates the boilerplate of manually committing and rolling back transactions in every controller. The library provides TransactionFilterAttribute — a global ASP.NET Core action filter that automatically:

  • Sets the isolation level before the controller action executes, when the action carries [TransactionIsolationLevel]
  • Commits on successful completion (pending changes are saved first)
  • Rolls back on exception or when the action returned a 4xx/5xx result

The filter does not open the transaction itself. The unit of work opens it lazily: on the first SaveChanges / SaveChangesAsync (the commit at the end of the action counts) or when you call BeginTransactionManually(). Queries executed before that moment run outside the transaction.

Optionally decorate an action with [TransactionIsolationLevel(IsolationLevel.Serializable)] to set a specific isolation level for that endpoint. The attribute is read from the action method only - placed on a controller class it has no effect.

// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.WebApiCore;

// 1. Register UoW + TransactionFilterAttribute
builder.Services
    .AddUnitOfWorkForWebApi<IApplicationDbContext, ApplicationDbContext>();

// 2. Register it as a global filter
builder.Services.AddControllers(options =>
{
    options.Filters.AddUnitOfWorkTransactionAttribute();
});

docs.title: Controller — transaction managed automatically
docs.text:
[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class OrdersController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IUnitOfWork<IApplicationDbContext> _uow;

    public OrdersController(IUnitOfWork<IApplicationDbContext> uow)
    {
        _uow = uow;
    }

    [HttpPost]
    public async Task<IActionResult> CreateOrder([FromBody] CreateOrderDto dto)
    {
        // You do not have to commit manually — TransactionFilter does it when the action completes
        var order = new Order { CustomerId = dto.CustomerId, Amount = dto.Amount };
        _uow.DataProvider.Orders.Add(order);
        await _uow.SaveChangesAsync();

        return CreatedAtAction(nameof(GetOrder), new { id = order.Id }, order);
    }

    // Endpoint with a higher isolation level — prevents phantom reads
    [HttpPost("transfer")]
    [TransactionIsolationLevel(System.Data.IsolationLevel.Serializable)]
    public async Task<IActionResult> TransferFunds([FromBody] TransferDto dto)
    {
        // Open the transaction now, so that the reads below run inside it
        // (otherwise it would open only on the first SaveChanges)
        _uow.BeginTransactionManually();

        var from = await _uow.DataProvider.Accounts.FindAsync(dto.FromId);
        var to = await _uow.DataProvider.Accounts.FindAsync(dto.ToId);

        from.Balance -= dto.Amount;
        to.Balance += dto.Amount;

        await _uow.SaveChangesAsync();
        return Ok();
    }
}

If the action throws an exception, TransactionFilterAttribute automatically calls RollbackTransaction(). Otherwise it calls CommitTransaction(), which saves pending changes before committing - an action that only adds or changes entities does not have to call SaveChanges itself.

docs.title: 🔒 Transaction consistency
docs.text:
• Rollback on error responses. The filter rolls back not only after an exception but also when the action returned a 4xx/5xx result (BadRequest, Conflict, StatusCode(500)). Partial writes made before return Conflict(...) are no longer persisted.
  • Commit failures stay visible. When both commit and rollback fail, ActionExecutedContext.Exception receives an AggregateException with both (previously the rollback exception replaced the root cause and escaped the filter).
  • UnitOfWork disposes the transaction in finally, so a failed commit never leaves an open transaction on the connection.
  • The transaction opens lazily. It starts on the first SaveChanges / SaveChangesAsync or on BeginTransactionManually(), not when the action starts. A read that must be protected by the transaction (check-then-write, for example) needs BeginTransactionManually() before it.
  • Supported isolation levels. The default is ReadCommitted. The unit of work supports ReadCommitted, ReadUncommitted and Serializable; any other level throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException when the database connection is opened.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This library standardizes exception handling in ASP.NET Core Web API applications. It solves the problem of inconsistent error responses: instead of raw stack traces or ad-hoc JSON, every error is converted to a unified ExceptionHandlingResultModel (errorCode, message, errors[]).

It provides two mechanisms:

  • Middleware (ConfigureExceptionHandler) - a global handler that intercepts unhandled exceptions for the whole application
  • Action filter (HandleExceptionAttribute + AddExceptionHandlingFilterAttribute) - returns the same structure for invalid ModelState at controller/action level

The shipped DefaultExceptionHandlingProvider maps FluentValidation ValidationException to 400 with per-field errors and every other exception to 500 with a generic message. You can implement your own IExceptionHandlingProvider to map domain exceptions to other HTTP codes.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling.Interfaces;
using TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling.Providers;
using TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling.WebApiCore;
using TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling.WebApiCore.Middleware;

// Built-in provider (400 for validation, 500 + generic message otherwise)
builder.Services
    .AddExceptionHandlingForWebApi<IExceptionHandlingProvider, DefaultExceptionHandlingProvider>();
// ...or your own provider:
// .AddExceptionHandlingForWebApi<IExceptionHandlingProvider, MyExceptionHandlingProvider>();

// Option A: global MVC filter (invalid ModelState -> structured 400)
builder.Services.AddControllers(options =>
{
    options.Filters.AddExceptionHandlingFilterAttribute();
});

// Option B: middleware (preferred for global handling of unhandled exceptions)
var app = builder.Build();
app.ConfigureExceptionHandler();

docs.text:
using FluentValidation;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ModelBinding;
using TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling.Interfaces;
using TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling.Model;

public class MyExceptionHandlingProvider : IExceptionHandlingProvider
{
    private readonly bool includeDetails;

    public MyExceptionHandlingProvider(IHostEnvironment env) => includeDetails = env.IsDevelopment();

    public ExceptionHandlingResultModel Response(Exception exception)
    {
        var root = exception.GetBaseException();
        return root switch
        {
            ValidationException ve => new ExceptionHandlingResultModel(400, ve.Message,
                ve.Errors.Select(e => new ExceptionOrValidationError(e.PropertyName, e.ErrorMessage))),

            NotFoundException nf => new ExceptionHandlingResultModel(404, nf.Message,
                new[] { new ExceptionOrValidationError("", nf.Message) }),

            UnauthorizedAccessException => new ExceptionHandlingResultModel(401, "Unauthorized",
                new[] { new ExceptionOrValidationError("", "Unauthorized") }),

            // Never echo root.Message outside Development: it may contain connection strings, paths or SQL.
            _ => new ExceptionHandlingResultModel(500,
                includeDetails ? root.Message : "An unexpected error occurred.",
                new[] { new ExceptionOrValidationError("", includeDetails ? root.Message : "An unexpected error occurred.") }),
        };
    }

    public ExceptionHandlingResultModel Response(ModelStateDictionary modelState)
        => new ExceptionHandlingResultModel(modelState);   // 400 "Validation Failed" + field errors
}

docs.title: Resulting JSON error response
docs.text:
{
  "message": "Validation Failed",
  "errorCode": 400,
  "errors": [
    { "field": "Email", "message": "Email address is required" },
    { "message": "Name must not be empty" }
  ]
}

The field property is omitted (WhenWritingNull) when the error is not tied to a specific field.

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• No exception details leak by default. DefaultExceptionHandlingProvider returns 500 with "An unexpected error occurred." for anything that is not a validation failure. The root-cause message is included only when the provider is created with IHostEnvironment in the Development environment, or explicitly with new DefaultExceptionHandlingProvider(includeExceptionDetails: true). Previously the innermost exception message (SQL errors, host names, file paths) was returned to every anonymous caller as HTTP 400.
  • Correct status codes. Server failures are 5xx, so alerting, load balancers and client retry policies see them as such. The middleware clamps the provider's ErrorCode to 400-599 and ExceptionOccuredResult honours the model's code instead of forcing 400.
  • Fail loudly on mis-configuration. The middleware resolves IExceptionHandlingService with GetRequiredService, so forgetting AddExceptionHandlingForWebApi produces a clear exception instead of a blank 500.
  • A client error is not a server error (3.0). An exception the provider answers with a 4xx status (validation, a missing resource) is not logged as An unhandled exception has occurred… at Error level and adds no error.type tag to the http.server.request.duration metric - alerts on server errors do not fire on bad client input. The exception is logged at Debug level in the TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling category. 5xx answers are logged as errors, as before; a 404 the provider chose is sent as a 404.

Exception handling and request validation for minimal APIs as endpoint filters, on top of ExceptionHandling: the same provider and the same JSON error model as the middleware and the MVC filter. The library is a package of its own; it changes nothing in the existing ones.

  • WithValidation<TRequest>() - before the endpoint is called, runs every registered FluentValidation validator for the argument of type TRequest. A failure is the provider's answer (400 with one entry per field by default) and the endpoint is not called.
  • WithExceptionHandling() - turns an exception of the endpoint (or of a whole group) into the provider's answer. Useful when only a part of the application should answer this way; for the whole application the middleware app.ConfigureExceptionHandler() is enough.
  • ToResult() - turns an ExceptionHandlingResultModel into a minimal-API result with the model's status.

NativeAOT

The library is safe for trimming and NativeAOT: the request type is a type parameter, so the filter uses no reflection. Checked natively in CI with a real FluentValidation validator (see Trimming and NativeAOT).

using TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling.MinimalApi;

public record NewProduct(string Name, decimal Price);

public class NewProductValidator : AbstractValidator<NewProduct>
{
    public NewProductValidator()
    {
        RuleFor(p => p.Name).NotEmpty();
        RuleFor(p => p.Price).GreaterThan(0);
    }
}

var products = app.MapGroup("/api/products").WithExceptionHandling();

// An invalid body -> 400 with the Name and Price fields; the endpoint is not called
products.MapPost("/", (NewProduct product) => Results.Created($"/api/products/{product.Name}", product))
        .WithValidation<NewProduct>();

// An exception -> the provider's answer (404 for KeyNotFoundException in a provider of your own, for example)
products.MapGet("/{id:int}", (int id) => Find(id) ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"Product {id} does not exist."));

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This library provides a ready-made set of pipeline behaviors for MediatR that cover the most common enterprise application needs: logging, validation, caching, fallback, and retry. Instead of manually implementing these cross-cutting concerns in every handler, register them once via PipelineRegistration and they apply to all requests.

Behaviors execute in order: Logging → Validation → Caching → Fallback → Retry → Handler.

The library supports auto-discovery (via Scrutor) — cache policies, fallback handlers, and retry configurations are automatically scanned and registered from the specified assembly.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.DI;

// Register MediatR
builder.Services.AddMediator(cfg =>
    cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly));

var pipeline = new PipelineRegistration(builder.Services);

// 1. The five pipeline behaviors + HybridCache
pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors();

// 2. Scan the assembly for ICachePolicy<,>, IFallbackHandler<,> and IRetryableRequest<,> implementations
pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors(typeof(Program).Assembly);

// Validators are not scanned by the library - register the ones you have
builder.Services.AddTransient<IValidator<GetProductQuery>, GetProductQueryValidator>();

Both RegisterPipelineBehaviors calls are needed. The parameterless overload registers the behaviors (and HybridCache) but no policies; the overload that takes an assembly only scans it and does not add the behaviors. Without the first call nothing runs in the pipeline; without the second no request is cached, retried or answered by a fallback, because the behaviors find no policy for it.

RegisterPipelineBehaviors() also registers the HybridCache in which CachingBehavior keeps responses. On its own it is an in-process cache; when an IDistributedCache (for example Redis) is registered, HybridCache uses it automatically as the level shared between instances:

builder.Services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(options => options.Configuration = "localhost:6379");

Changes in 3.0 (test phase)

The TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR* libraries use ForkForward.Mediator - a fork of MediatR 12.5.0 under the Apache-2.0 licence - instead of the MediatR package. The types and the behaviour are the same; in the application replace using MediatR; with using ForkForward.Mediator; and AddMediatR(...) with AddMediator(...). Details: Upgrading to 3.0.

Changes in 2.0

CachingBehavior uses HybridCache. The ICache interface and the Cache class are removed together with the Newtonsoft.Json dependency — delete your own ICache registration. Responses are serialized with System.Text.Json, and ICachePolicy.SlidingExpiration is no longer supported (an entry lives until it expires). After upgrading, clear the shared cache or change the key prefix: entries written by 1.x have a different format.

When the host registers an IDistributedCache (Redis, for example), responses are shared between application instances: an instance without the entry in memory reads it from the distributed cache without calling the handler. When the distributed cache cannot be reached, the handler answers the request - a cache outage does not stop requests.

// Request
public class GetProductQuery : IRequest<ProductDto>
{
    public int ProductId { get; set; }
}

// Validator (run by ValidationBehavior once it is registered in DI as IValidator<GetProductQuery>)
public class GetProductQueryValidator : AbstractValidator<GetProductQuery>
{
    public GetProductQueryValidator()
    {
        RuleFor(x => x.ProductId).GreaterThan(0);
    }
}

// Handler
public class GetProductQueryHandler : IRequestHandler<GetProductQuery, ProductDto>
{
    private readonly IProductRepository _repo;

    public GetProductQueryHandler(IProductRepository repo) => _repo = repo;

    public async Task<ProductDto> Handle(GetProductQuery request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var product = await _repo.GetByIdAsync(request.ProductId, ct);
        return product?.ToDto() ?? throw new NotFoundException($"Product {request.ProductId} not found");
    }
}

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• The cache key carries no request data. The default ICachePolicy.GetCacheKey builds {RequestType.FullName}:{SHA-256 of the request JSON} (CacheKeyGenerator.Generate). The previous Prop:ToString() format gave requests that differed only in collection contents (CustomerIds = [1] vs [2]) the same key, returning another caller's data.
  • The key does not include the caller's identity. For per-user or per-tenant data override GetCacheKey and prefix the key with the caller id, otherwise one user's response is served to another.
  • LoggingBehavior does not serialize the request. Only the request type name and a correlation id go into the logging scope; passwords, tokens and binary payloads never reach the logs.
  • A validation refusal is not an error. A ValidationException is logged at Information level (rejected by validation …; invalid: Id) with the property names only - validation messages can quote the values the client sent. A request cancelled by its caller is logged as Information too; every other handler exception as Error. The exception is always rethrown.

Logging → Validation → Caching → Fallback → Retry → Handler

```csharp

public class MyQueryValidator : AbstractValidator<MyQuery>
{
    public MyQueryValidator() { RuleFor(x => x.Id).GreaterThan(0); }
```

```csharp

{
    public string GetCacheKey(MyQuery r) => $"my:{r.Id}";
    public TimeSpan? AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow => TimeSpan.FromHours(1);
    public TimeSpan? LocalCacheExpiration => TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
    public IReadOnlyCollection<string>? Tags => ["products"];
}
```

### Fallback and retry
```csharp
public class MyFallback : IFallbackHandler<MyQuery, MyResponse>
{
    public Task<MyResponse> HandleFallback(MyQuery request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        => Task.FromResult(MyResponse.Empty);
}

public class MyRetry : IRetryableRequest<MyQuery, MyResponse>
{
    public int RetryAttempts => 3;                       // default 1
    public int ExceptionsAllowedBeforeCircuitTrip => 5;  // default 1
}
```

- Call both RegisterPipelineBehaviors() and RegisterPipelineBehaviors(assembly): the first adds the behaviors, the second only scans for policies
- ValidationBehavior runs the IValidator<TRequest> instances registered in DI - the library does not register validators, do it yourself
- For the cache to work, implement ICachePolicy<TRequest, TResponse> in the scanned assembly (or register it yourself)
- IFallbackHandler has one method: HandleFallback(request, cancellationToken) - the exception is not passed to it
- LoggingBehavior: start and finish at Debug, validation refusals and cancellations at Information, handler failures at Error - do not count validation failures from Error entries
- Every request has a unique correlation ID in the logs
- The default cache key is a hash of the request content; for per-user data override GetCacheKey and add the user/tenant id
- LoggingBehavior logs only the request name and correlation id - log request fields explicitly in the handler, never whole objects with secrets
- Caching is built on HybridCache (registered by RegisterPipelineBehaviors): do not register ICache - that interface does not exist in 2.0
- Every response is cached as returned - including null, 0 and false; concurrent identical requests run the handler once
- Set an entry's lifetime with AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow (5 minutes by default) or AbsoluteExpiration; SlidingExpiration is not supported
- A cached response type must be serializable with System.Text.Json; register an IHybridCacheSerializer<T> for other types

docs.text:
A lightweight package defining ICachableRequest<TResponse> — a contract for MediatR requests that name their own cache key. A request implementing this interface provides a GetCacheKey() method that generates a unique cache key for that particular query instance.

The package contains the contract only: it has no services and nothing to register. CachingBehavior from TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR does not read ICachableRequest<TResponse> — it caches a request only when an ICachePolicy<TRequest, TResponse> is registered for it. Use the interface to keep the key logic in the request itself, and add a cache policy that returns that key (shown below) when the response is to be cached by that behavior.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.Caching

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.Caching;
using ForkForward.Mediator;

// Request with built-in cache key logic
public class GetUserProfileQuery : ICachableRequest<UserProfileDto>
{
    public int UserId { get; set; }
    public string Language { get; set; } = "pl";

    // Unique key that takes the query parameters into account
    public string GetCacheKey() => $"user-profile:{UserId}:{Language}";
}

// Handler — standard MediatR
public class GetUserProfileQueryHandler : IRequestHandler<GetUserProfileQuery, UserProfileDto>
{
    private readonly IUserRepository _repo;

    public GetUserProfileQueryHandler(IUserRepository repo) => _repo = repo;

    public async Task<UserProfileDto> Handle(GetUserProfileQuery request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var user = await _repo.GetByIdAsync(request.UserId, ct);
        return user.ToProfileDto(request.Language);
    }
}

docs.title: Caching the request with CachingBehavior
docs.text:
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.Interfaces.Caching;

// The policy is what CachingBehavior looks for; it hands back the key the request defines
public class GetUserProfileQueryCachePolicy : ICachePolicy<GetUserProfileQuery, UserProfileDto>
{
    public string GetCacheKey(GetUserProfileQuery request) => request.GetCacheKey();
}

Integration with CachingBehavior

ICachableRequest is a marker interface — on its own it does not trigger caching, and CachingBehavior from the TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR package does not look at it. A request is cached only when an ICachePolicy<TRequest, TResponse> is registered for it (PipelineRegistration.RegisterPipelineBehaviors(assembly) scans for policies). Without a policy the request above runs its handler every time.

MediatR pipeline integration for email sending. The library provides the SendMail command and its SendMailCommandHandler, making email sending a natural part of CQRS architecture — you can send an email via _mediator.Send(new SendMail { ... }) without a direct dependency on IEmailProvider.

This approach makes it easy to enrich the sending process with logging, retry, and auditing from the pipeline behaviors level, without modifying the handler.

docs.title: Installation

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.Email;
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.Email.Handlers;
using TailoredApps.Shared.Email.MailMessageBuilder;

// 1. Register the email provider (SMTP or console)
builder.Services.RegisterSmtpProvider();

// 2. Register the mail message builder
builder.Services.AddTransient<IMailMessageBuilder, TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilder>();
builder.Services.Configure<TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilderOptions>(o =>
{
    o.Location = "EmailTemplates/";
    o.FileExtension = "html";
});

// 3. MediatR: scan the library assembly as well - that is where SendMailCommandHandler lives
builder.Services.AddMediator(cfg =>
{
    cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly);
    cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(SendMailCommandHandler).Assembly);
});

The package has no registration extension of its own. MediatR resolves the handler as IRequestHandler<SendMail, SendMailResponse>, so registering SendMailCommandHandler only under ISendMailCommandHandler does not let _mediator.Send(new SendMail { ... }) find it. Either scan the library assembly as above or register the handler under the MediatR interface yourself:

builder.Services.AddTransient<IRequestHandler<SendMail, SendMailResponse>, SendMailCommandHandler>();

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.Email.Messages.Commands;

public class UserRegistrationService
{
    private readonly IMediator _mediator;

    public UserRegistrationService(IMediator mediator) => _mediator = mediator;

    public async Task RegisterUserAsync(string email, string userName)
    {
        // Registration logic...

        // Send the welcome email through the MediatR pipeline
        var result = await _mediator.Send(new SendMail
        {
            Recipent = email,
            Subject = "Welcome to our service!",
            Template = "welcome.html",
            TemplateVariables = new Dictionary<string, string>
            {
                { "UserName", userName },
                { "ActivationUrl", $"https://app.example.com/activate/{Guid.NewGuid()}" }
            },
            Attachments = null
        });

        Console.WriteLine($"Email sent, MessageId: {result.MessageId}");
    }

    public async Task SendInvoiceAsync(
        string email,
        string invoiceNumber,
        byte[] pdfContent)
    {
        await _mediator.Send(new SendMail
        {
            Recipent = email,
            Subject = $"Invoice #{invoiceNumber}",
            Template = "invoice.html",
            TemplateVariables = new Dictionary<string, string>
            {
                { "InvoiceNumber", invoiceNumber }
            },
            Attachments = new Dictionary<string, byte[]>
            {
                { $"invoice_{invoiceNumber}.pdf", pdfContent }
            }
        });
    }
}

This library integrates ML.NET image classification with the MediatR pipeline. It provides ready-made commands (ClassifyImage, TrainImageClassificationModel) and their handlers, making image classification a first-class citizen in CQRS architecture.

Under the hood, ImageClassificationService uses ML.NET with a PredictionEnginePool for efficient concurrent inference. The library also supports in-app model training — you can train a new model by providing a labeled image dataset.

// Program.cs
using Microsoft.Extensions.ML;
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.ImageClassification.Infrastructure;
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.ImageClassification.Interfaces.Domain.Models;

// MediatR: the handlers of both commands live in the library assembly, so scan it as well
builder.Services.AddMediator(cfg =>
{
    cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly);
    cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(AddPredictionEngineExtension).Assembly);
});

// Library services + the ML.NET PredictionEnginePool with the model
builder.Services.AddPredictionEngine(config =>
{
    config.RegisterMachineLearningModel<InMemoryImageData, ImagePredictionScore>(pool =>
    {
        pool.FromFile(builder.Configuration[ImageClassificationOptions.ModelFilePathConfig]!);
    });
});

AddPredictionEngine registers IImageClassificationService, IModelInfoService and IModelHelper (scoped) and binds ImageClassificationOptions. It does not register the MediatR handlers - that is what scanning the library assembly is for. RegisterMachineLearningModel adds the ML.NET PredictionEnginePool; where the model is loaded from is decided by the pool builder (FromFile above). Register the model without a name: predictions use the default model of the pool.

The types live in the namespace TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.ImageClassification, not under the package name.

public class ImageAnalysisController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IMediator _mediator;

    public ImageAnalysisController(IMediator mediator) => _mediator = mediator;
