```csharp
    cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly);
    cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(AddPredictionEngineExtension).Assembly); // handlers of the library
});
builder.Services.AddPredictionEngine(config =>
    config.RegisterMachineLearningModel<InMemoryImageData, ImagePredictionScore>(pool =>
        pool.FromFile(builder.Configuration[ImageClassificationOptions.ModelFilePathConfig]!)));
```

### What gets configured
- IImageClassificationService, IModelInfoService, IModelHelper (scoped) and ImageClassificationOptions
- The ML.NET PredictionEnginePool<InMemoryImageData, ImagePredictionScore> with the model (default, unnamed)
- The handlers of ClassifyImage and TrainImageClassificationModel - only through the MediatR scan of the library assembly

### Configuration (section "ImageClassification")
- ModelFilePath - the model file (used for the model metadata and by the registration above)
- TrainingRoot, ModelsRoot - directories training sets are read from / models are written to; required for training
- MaxImageBytes - image size limit for ClassifyImage, default 10485760 (10 MB), 0 = no limit

### Image classification
```csharp
var result = await _mediator.Send(new ClassifyImage
{
    FileByteArray = imageBytes,
    FileName = "photo.jpg"
});
// result.ImagePrediction.PredictedLabel  — the predicted class
// result.ImagePrediction.PredictedScore  — confidence (0-1)
```

### Model training
```csharp
var result = await _mediator.Send(new TrainImageClassificationModel
{
    Source = "pets",                   // inside TrainingRoot; subfolders = class names
    ModelDestFolderPath = "pets.zip"   // model file inside ModelsRoot
});
// result.ModelPath, result.ModelVersion, result.Labels, result.ModelInfo (metrics as text)
```

### Rules
- The namespace is TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.ImageClassification, not the package name
- AddMediator must scan the library assembly - AddPredictionEngine does not register the handlers
- The model must be a ZIP file (ML.NET format)
- The `ImageClassification` configuration section is required — a missing section throws `InvalidOperationException` when the options are first used
- The model version and labels are stored in the archive as separate `Version.txt` and `Labels.txt` entries
- Training folder: each subfolder = one class, folder name = label
- PredictionEnginePool is thread-safe — safe for concurrent use
- PredictedScore ∈ [0,1] — the closer to 1, the higher the model's confidence
- Configure ImageClassification:TrainingRoot and ImageClassification:ModelsRoot - training rejects paths outside those directories
- ClassifyImage accepts only JPEG/PNG up to MaxImageBytes (default 10 MB); larger or foreign files throw ArgumentException
- Expose the training command to administrators only - it starts a long TensorFlow job on the given data

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This library provides a base PagedAndSortedRequest<TResponse, TQuery, TModel> class for MediatR requests that require pagination and sorting. It standardizes paging (Page, Count) and sorting (SortField, SortDir) parameters across all list queries in the application.

The class is tightly integrated with TailoredApps.Shared.Querying — requires TQuery to inherit from QueryBase and TResponse to implement IPagedResult<TModel>.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.PagedRequest

docs.title: Defining the query filter, response and request
docs.text:
using TailoredApps.Shared.Querying;
using TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.PagedRequest;

// 1. The filter inherits from QueryBase
public class ProductFilter : QueryBase
{
    public string NameContains { get; set; }
    public decimal? MinPrice { get; set; }
    public decimal? MaxPrice { get; set; }
    public bool? InStock { get; set; }
}

// 2. The response implements IPagedResult<TModel>
public class ProductListResponse : IPagedResult<ProductDto>
{
    public ICollection<ProductDto> Results { get; set; }
    public int Count { get; set; }
}

// 3. The request inherits from PagedAndSortedRequest
public class GetProductsQuery
    : PagedAndSortedRequest<ProductListResponse, ProductFilter, ProductDto>
{
    // All paging/sorting parameters are inherited
    // You can add your own properties:
    public bool IncludeArchived { get; set; } = false;
}

docs.title: Handler
docs.text:
The handler uses ApplySorting and PagingAsync from the TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework package. Both accept the request directly (it implements ISortingParameters and IPagingParameters) and validate the values the client sent.

using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.Querying;

public class GetProductsQueryHandler
    : IRequestHandler<GetProductsQuery, ProductListResponse>
{
    private readonly IProductRepository _repo;

    public GetProductsQueryHandler(IProductRepository repo) => _repo = repo;

    public async Task<ProductListResponse> Handle(
        GetProductsQuery request,
        CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var query = _repo.AsQueryable();

        // Apply the filters
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.Filter?.NameContains))
            query = query.Where(p => p.Name.Contains(request.Filter.NameContains));

        if (request.Filter?.MinPrice.HasValue == true)
            query = query.Where(p => p.Price >= request.Filter.MinPrice.Value);

        // Sorting: SortField comes from the client, so it is checked against an allow-list.
        // Paging: validates Page and Count, counts all matching rows and reads one page
        // (the whole result when the request carries no paging values).
        var page = await query
            .ApplySorting(request, allowedSortFields: new[] { "Name", "Price" })
            .PagingAsync(request);

        return new ProductListResponse
        {
            Results = page.Results.Select(p => p.ToDto()).ToList(),
            Count = page.Count   // total number of matching rows
        };
    }
}

docs.title: Calling from a controller
docs.text:
[HttpGet]
public async Task<IActionResult> GetProducts([FromQuery] GetProductsQuery query)
{
    // GET /api/products?page=1&count=20&sortField=Price&sortDir=Asc&filter.nameContains=shirt
    var result = await _mediator.Send(query);
    return Ok(result);
}

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text: Page, Count and SortField come straight from the HTTP request. The EF layer (PagingQuery<T>, ApplySorting) enforces Page >= 1, 1 <= Count <= PagingQuery<T>.MaxPageSize (default 1000) and a single property name as the sort field; violations throw ArgumentException/ArgumentOutOfRangeException. For entities with sensitive columns pass an allow-list of sort fields to ApplySorting.

You are using PagedAndSortedRequest as the base class for paged MediatR requests.

### Definition
```csharp
// Filter
public class MyFilter : QueryBase { public string Name { get; set; } }

// Response

{
    public ICollection<MyDto> Results { get; set; }
    public int Count { get; set; }
}

```

### URL parameters (ASP.NET Core binding)
?page=1&count=20&sortField=Name&sortDir=Asc&filter.name=test

### In the handler
```csharp
// using TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework.Querying;  (package TailoredApps.Shared.EntityFramework)
var page = await query
    .ApplySorting(request, allowedSortFields: new[] { "Name" })   // validates SortField

// page.Results - the items of the page, page.Count - the total
```

- TQuery must inherit from QueryBase
- TResponse must implement IPagedResult<TModel>

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This library provides a unified abstraction for payment gateway integration in .NET applications. Instead of writing separate logic for each payment operator, you program against the common IPaymentService interface, which automatically routes requests to the correct provider based on its key ("Stripe", "PayU", "CashBill", etc.).

Key architectural elements:

  • IPaymentProvider — contract for each provider (channels, payment initiation, status, webhook)
  • IWebhookPaymentProvider — extension for providers supporting webhooks with signature verification
  • IPaymentService — facade aggregating all registered providers
  • PaymentOptionsBuilder — fluent API for registering providers in DI

TailoredApps.Shared.Payments is the core — concrete provider implementations are in separate TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Provider.* packages.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Payments

# Add the selected providers:
dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Provider.Stripe
dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Provider.PayU
dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Provider.CashBill

docs.title: DI registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.Payments;
using TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Provider.Stripe;
using TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Provider.PayU;

builder.Services
    .AddPayments()
    .RegisterStripeProvider()
    .RegisterPayUProvider();

Every provider package has a Register<Name>Provider() method on the builder returned by AddPayments(): it registers the provider's dependencies (options from configuration, the HTTP client, webhook handling) and adds the provider to IPaymentService. The calls chain.

RegisterPaymentProvider<T>() is for plugging in your own IPaymentProvider implementation. For the providers from the packages that call alone is not enough - it does not register their dependencies. The former two-step form (builder.Services.RegisterStripeProvider(); plus AddPayments().RegisterPaymentProvider<StripeProvider>()) still works.

docs.title: Initiating a payment
docs.text:
public class CheckoutService
{
    private readonly IPaymentService _payments;

    public CheckoutService(IPaymentService payments) => _payments = payments;

    public async Task<string> CreatePaymentAsync(CartDto cart, string email)
    {
        var response = await _payments.RegisterPayment(new PaymentRequest
        {
            PaymentProvider = "Stripe",       // or "PayU", "CashBill" etc.
            PaymentChannel = "card",
            PaymentModel = PaymentModel.OneTime,
            Title = $"Order #{cart.OrderId}",
            Description = "Purchase in the MyShop store",
            Currency = "PLN",
            Amount = cart.TotalAmount,
            Email = email,
            FirstName = cart.CustomerFirstName,
            Surname = cart.CustomerLastName
        });

        // Redirect the user to the payment page
        return response.RedirectUrl;
    }

    public async Task<PaymentStatusEnum?> CheckStatusAsync(string providerId, string paymentId)
    {
        try
        {
            var response = await _payments.GetStatus(providerId, paymentId);
            return response.PaymentStatus;
        }
        catch (HttpRequestException)   // a failing gateway (covers PaymentGatewayException)
        {
            return null;               // unknown state: leave the order alone, check again later
        }
    }
}

PaymentProvider, Amount and Currency are required members: an object initializer that leaves one out does not compile (CS9035), and System.Text.Json refuses a document without them (JsonException, a 400 response in an API controller). The shorter form is the constructor new PaymentRequest("Stripe", cart.TotalAmount, "PLN") { Title = "…" }. RegisterPayment also refuses a blank provider key or currency (ArgumentException) and an amount of zero or less (ArgumentOutOfRangeException) before it calls the gateway.

Breaking change (2.0): code that creates a PaymentRequest without one of these three members no longer compiles.

docs.title: Handling webhooks
docs.text:
[ApiController]
[Route("api/webhooks/payments")]
public class PaymentWebhookController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IPaymentService _payments;

    public PaymentWebhookController(IPaymentService payments) => _payments = payments;

    [HttpPost("{providerKey}")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> HandleWebhook(
        string providerKey,
        [FromBody] JsonElement body)
    {
        var request = new PaymentWebhookRequest
        {
            Body = body.GetRawText(),
            Headers = Request.Headers.ToDictionary(h => h.Key, h => h.Value),
            Query = Request.Query.ToDictionary(q => q.Key, q => q.Value)
        };

        var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync(providerKey, request, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        return result switch
        {
            PaymentWebhookProcessed => Ok(),
            PaymentWebhookIgnored => NoContent(),
            PaymentWebhookRejected { Rejection: PaymentWebhookRejection.InvalidSignature } => Unauthorized(),
            PaymentWebhookRejected => BadRequest(),
        };
    }
}

docs.title: Startup validation of configuration
docs.text:
Every Register*Provider() checks the settings the provider cannot work without: its API credentials and the secret that signs its webhooks. If one is missing the host does not start — the OptionsValidationException names every missing setting (for example 'Payments:Providers:PayU:SignatureKey' is not configured.). Return and notification URLs are not validated.

Provider (Payments:Providers:<Name>) Required settings Adyen ApiKey, MerchantAccount, NotificationHmacKey CashBill (Payments:Providers:Cashbill) ServiceUrl, ShopId, ShopSecretPhrase HotPay SecretHash PayNow ApiKey, SignatureKey PayU ClientId, ClientSecret, PosId, SignatureKey Przelewy24 MerchantId, PosId, ApiKey, CrcKey Revolut ApiKey, WebhookSecret Stripe SecretKey, WebhookSecret Tpay ClientId, ClientSecret, SecurityCode

Register only the providers you actually use and have configured in the given environment.

docs.text: Method Description services.AddPayments() Registers IPaymentService/PaymentService builder.Register<Name>Provider() Registers a provider from a package (its dependencies + adding it to IPaymentService), e.g. RegisterTpayProvider(); returns the builder builder.RegisterPaymentProvider<T>() Adds your own IPaymentProvider implementation

docs.title: ⚠️ A failing gateway is not a refusal
docs.text:
Rejected means only what the gateway said: the payment was declined or cancelled, or the request to create a payment was refused (4xx). When the gateway gives no usable answer, the provider throws PaymentGatewayException - the state of the payment is then not known and an order must not be cancelled on that basis.

Situation Outcome Creating a payment, the gateway answers 5xx, 408 or 429 PaymentGatewayException (IsTransient == true) Creating a payment, the gateway answers another 4xx PaymentResponse with status Rejected and the error text in ResponseObject Status or token query, an answer outside 2xx PaymentGatewayException The gateway cannot be reached HttpRequestException (the base class of PaymentGatewayException) Timeout TaskCanceledException 
try
{
    var payment = await _payments.GetStatus("Tpay", paymentId, cancellationToken);
    if (payment.PaymentStatus == PaymentStatusEnum.Rejected)
        await _orders.CancelAsync(orderId, cancellationToken);   // the gateway answered: declined
}
catch (HttpRequestException exception)   // covers PaymentGatewayException
{
    // The state of the payment is not known: leave the order as it is and check again later.
    _logger.LogWarning(exception, "Gateway unavailable for payment {PaymentId}", paymentId);
}

PaymentGatewayException carries Provider, StatusCode, IsTransient and the beginning of the gateway's answer in ResponseBody (the text is kept out of Message because it may hold details of the request). It applies to all nine providers. From 3.0 Stripe turns the SDK's StripeException into PaymentGatewayException (the original in InnerException) and returns a 4xx refusal as Rejected; in 2.x it let StripeException through. CashBill threw WebException up to 2.0.1.

Payments and the HTTP providers (all but Stripe) are safe for trimming and NativeAOT - see Trimming and NativeAOT.

Przelewy24: when a transaction cannot be verified during a webhook, the result is PaymentWebhookRejected (ProcessingFailed), not a processed payment that was rejected - answer with a status outside 2xx and Przelewy24 sends the notification again.

Breaking change (2.0): until now a failed status query returned Rejected (Revolut: Created), and a 5xx while creating a payment returned Rejected or threw JsonException.

docs.title: 🔒 Webhook security
docs.text:
• Fail-closed. Every provider rejects a notification when its secret (HMAC key, SignatureKey, CrcKey, SecurityCode, ShopSecretPhrase, WebhookSecret) is not configured or the signature is empty. Previously an empty secret meant a signature computed with an empty key, which anyone could reproduce.
  • Constant-time comparison. Signatures are compared with WebhookSignature.FixedTimeEquals / FixedTimeEqualsIgnoreCase (TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Security), so response timing does not leak the expected value. Use these helpers in custom providers.
  • Case-insensitive headers and query. PaymentWebhookRequest.Headers/Query resolve stripe-signature and Stripe-Signature alike - HTTP/2 lower-cases header names.
  • Identifiers in URLs. PaymentIdentifier.EnsureSafe rejects identifiers containing /, ?, #, whitespace etc. before they are placed in a gateway request URL (prevents re-targeting an authenticated request to another endpoint).
  • Error messages never disclose the signature. PaymentWebhookResult.ErrorMessage carries a short description ("Invalid signature.") and never the expected value.
  • Webhook results identify the payment. PaymentResponse.PaymentUniqueId is populated from the payload (orderId, paymentId, sessionId, merchantReference, order_id, transactionId) - de-duplicate events on it. Non-terminal events (Processing) are returned as Ignore.

docs.text:
## TailoredApps.Shared.Payments - instructions for an AI agent

You use TailoredApps.Shared.Payments to integrate with payment gateways.

### Registration
```csharp
builder.Services.AddPayments()
    .RegisterStripeProvider()
    .RegisterPayUProvider();
```

### Initiating a payment
```csharp
var response = await _payments.RegisterPayment(new PaymentRequest
{
    PaymentProvider = "Stripe",   // provider key
    PaymentChannel = "card",
    Currency = "PLN",
    Amount = 99.99m,
    Email = "user@example.com",
    Title = "Order #123"
});
string redirectUrl = response.RedirectUrl;  // → browser
```

### Checking the status
```csharp
try
{
    var status = await _payments.GetStatus("Stripe", paymentId);
    // status.PaymentStatus: Created/Processing/Finished/Rejected
}
catch (HttpRequestException)
{
    // a failing gateway: the state of the payment is not known - leave the order alone, check again later
}
```

### Handling webhooks
```csharp
var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync(providerKey, new PaymentWebhookRequest
{
    Body = rawBody,
    Headers = httpHeaders,
    Query = query
});

var response = result switch
{
    PaymentWebhookProcessed processed => Handle(processed.Payment),   // PaymentUniqueId + PaymentStatus
    PaymentWebhookIgnored => NoContent(),                             // authentic, nothing to do
    PaymentWebhookRejected { Rejection: PaymentWebhookRejection.InvalidSignature } => Unauthorized(),
    PaymentWebhookRejected => BadRequest(),
};
```

### Rules
- Every provider has a unique Key (e.g. "Stripe", "PayU", "CashBill")
- Register a provider from a package with one call on the builder: AddPayments().Register<Name>Provider(); RegisterPaymentProvider<T>() is for your own implementations
- PaymentRequest: always set PaymentProvider, Amount (greater than zero) and Currency - they are required; leaving one out is compile error CS9035
- Catch HttpRequestException (covers PaymentGatewayException) around RegisterPayment and GetStatus: a failing gateway means an unknown state - do not cancel the order, check again later
- Treat Rejected as a refusal only when the call returned without an exception
- A webhook result is always one of three records: PaymentWebhookProcessed (act on Payment), PaymentWebhookIgnored (answer 2xx, do nothing), PaymentWebhookRejected (trust nothing in the request)
- Read the rejection reason from PaymentWebhookRejected.Rejection (e.g. InvalidSignature -> 401, MalformedPayload -> 400) - never parse the Message text
- Do not add a default branch to a switch over the result: the hierarchy is closed and the C# 15 compiler checks completeness
- The Amount is in the base currency (not in grosze — unless the provider requires otherwise)
- Webhooks require an HTTP POST endpoint with the raw body
- Never run a provider without its webhook secret configured - verification rejects every notification (fail-closed)
- In custom providers compare signatures with WebhookSignature.FixedTimeEquals and pass URL identifiers through PaymentIdentifier.EnsureSafe
- Do not echo the webhook ErrorMessage to the caller - log it server-side
- De-duplicate events on PaymentUniqueId; the webhook consumer must be idempotent
- Register only configured providers: missing credentials or a missing webhook secret stop the application at startup (OptionsValidationException)
- Pass a CancellationToken (HttpContext.RequestAborted in a controller) to every IPaymentService call - it reaches the gateway HTTP calls
- Custom provider: every asynchronous method takes CancellationToken cancellationToken = default and forwards it to HttpClient

docs.title: Payment and reading the outcome
docs.text:
The provider creates a Hosted Checkout session (POST /sessions with mode: hosted): RegisterPayment returns the session id in PaymentUniqueId and the address of Adyen's payment page in RedirectUrl.

// 1. create the payment and send the shopper to the Adyen page
var response = await _payments.RegisterPayment(new PaymentRequest("Adyen", 49.99m, "PLN")
{
    AdditionalData = orderNumber,   // comes back as merchantReference in the webhook
}, cancellationToken);
await _orders.SavePaymentSessionAsync(orderNumber, response.PaymentUniqueId, cancellationToken);
return Redirect(response.RedirectUrl);

// 2. the shopper returns to ReturnUrl; Adyen appends sessionId and sessionResult to the address
[HttpGet("payment/return")]
public async Task<IActionResult> Return(string sessionId, string sessionResult, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    var payment = await _payments.GetStatus("Adyen", AdyenProvider.SessionResultId(sessionId, sessionResult), cancellationToken);
    return payment.PaymentStatus == PaymentStatusEnum.Finished ? View("Paid") : View("Pending");
}
Adyen session status PaymentStatus completed Finished paymentPending Processing refused, canceled, expired Rejected active (the shopper has not paid yet) Created
  • Adyen reports the outcome of a session only together with the sessionResult value it appends to the return address. GetStatus with a bare session id fails with ArgumentException - apart from the shopper's return, the webhook is the only source of the outcome.
  • The outcome read on return is for showing a thank-you page; settle the order on the webhook.
  • What was verified: the request and the response follow the Checkout OpenAPI v71 specification (the mode and url fields, GET /sessions/{sessionId}?sessionResult=); the names of the parameters appended to the return address come from the Hosted Checkout documentation and - like the whole provider - have not been exercised in the Adyen test environment.

docs.title: Webhook
docs.text:
A standard Adyen webhook is JSON with a notificationItems array; each NotificationRequestItem carries its own signature in additionalData.hmacSignature - there is no signature header. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 (key: NotificationHmacKey decoded from hex, output in Base64) over eight fields of the item joined with a colon; an absent field is an empty string:

pspReference:originalReference:merchantAccountCode:merchantReference:amount.value:amount.currency:eventCode:success

In the Adyen Customer Area (Developers → Webhooks) enable HMAC signing for the webhook and copy the generated key into NotificationHmacKey.

[HttpPost("webhooks/adyen")]
public async Task<IActionResult> AdyenWebhook(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    using var reader = new StreamReader(Request.Body, Encoding.UTF8);
    var body = await reader.ReadToEndAsync(cancellationToken);

    var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync("Adyen", new PaymentWebhookRequest
    {
        Body = body,
        ContentType = Request.ContentType,
        Headers = Request.Headers.ToDictionary(h => h.Key, h => h.Value),
    }, cancellationToken);

    // Adyen repeats the notification until it gets a 2xx response.
    return result is PaymentWebhookRejected ? Unauthorized() : Content(AdyenProvider.Acknowledgement, "text/plain");
}
eventCode success Result AUTHORISATION, REFUND true PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Finished AUTHORISATION, REFUND anything else / absent PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Rejected CANCELLATION, AUTHORISATION_FAILED any PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Rejected another event any PaymentWebhookIgnored (status Processing) - still acknowledge it

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• Verification fails closed: an empty or non-hex NotificationHmacKey, a missing additionalData.hmacSignature or a signature that does not match → PaymentWebhookRejection.InvalidSignature; a body that is not JSON or has no NotificationRequestItem → MalformedPayload. Constant-time comparison.
  • The signature covers eight fields, not the whole body: the other fields of the item (for example paymentMethod, reason) are not authenticated - do not base decisions on them.
  • A missing success field is treated as failure.
  • The webhook result carries PaymentUniqueId (merchantReference, falling back to pspReference) and ResponseObject = [accepted].
  • The first item of notificationItems is handled (Adyen sends one item per request).
  • What was verified: the implementation reproduces the example in Adyen's documentation (the key, the signed text and the expected signature are in the tests); send a test notification from the Adyen Customer Area before going live.

docs.title: Webhook
docs.text:
CashBill sends a GET/POST notification with three query-string parameters: cmd, args (the payment id) and sign. The provider has no option for the notification address. It reads the parameters from PaymentWebhookRequest.Query (not from the body or the headers), checks that sign equals MD5(cmd + args + ShopSecretPhrase) and then reads the current status of the payment from the CashBill API.

[AcceptVerbs("GET", "POST", Route = "webhooks/cashbill")]
public async Task<IActionResult> CashBillWebhook(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync("Cashbill", new PaymentWebhookRequest
    {
        HttpMethod = Request.Method,
        Query = Request.Query.ToDictionary(q => q.Key, q => q.Value),
    }, cancellationToken);

    return result is PaymentWebhookRejected ? BadRequest() : Ok();
}
Notification Result valid signature PaymentWebhookProcessed with the status read from CashBill (Created, Processing, Finished or Rejected) args missing PaymentWebhookRejected (MalformedPayload) sign missing or wrong PaymentWebhookRejected (InvalidSignature) ShopSecretPhrase not configured PaymentWebhookRejected (NotConfigured)

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• API calls go through HttpClient - the named client CashBill (CashbillHttpClient.HttpClientName) from IHttpClientFactory, so the handlers, resilience and timeouts configured in the host apply. An answer outside 2xx throws PaymentGatewayException (up to 2.0.1: WebException) - catch HttpRequestException. Failures are logged with the address but without the query string, which carries the request signature.
  • The notification signature is MD5(cmd + args + ShopSecretPhrase), compared in constant time. Both HandleWebhookAsync and the legacy TransactionStatusChange verify it - an invalid signature yields PaymentWebhookRejected (InvalidSignature, message "Invalid signature.") / a Rejected response without polling the CashBill API.
  • The error message no longer contains the expected signature (it used to be an oracle for forging arbitrary notifications).
  • Missing ShopSecretPhrase → PaymentWebhookRejected (NotConfigured, message "Signature verification is not configured.").
  • GetStatus(paymentId) rejects identifiers with special characters (PaymentIdentifier.EnsureSafe).
  • A webhook with a valid signature always gives PaymentWebhookProcessed with the status polled from CashBill - never PaymentWebhookIgnored. Check Payment.PaymentStatus before acting: it can still be Created or Processing.
  • After creating a payment the provider rewrites its return address to {ReturnUrl}/{paymentId}: the payer comes back to ReturnUrl with the payment id appended.

docs.text: The provider obtains an OAuth2 token (client_credentials) for every RegisterPayment and GetStatus call. The token is not cached.

docs.title: Webhook
docs.text:
PayU sends POST notifications with the OpenPayU-Signature header (signature=...;algorithm=...). The provider hashes the raw body followed by SignatureKey with the algorithm the header names - MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 (MD5 when it names none) - and compares the result with signature.

[HttpPost("webhooks/payu")]
public async Task<IActionResult> PayUWebhook(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    // The signature covers the exact bytes of the body - read it raw, not through [FromBody].
    using var reader = new StreamReader(Request.Body, Encoding.UTF8);
    var body = await reader.ReadToEndAsync(cancellationToken);

    var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync("PayU", new PaymentWebhookRequest
    {
        Body = body,
        ContentType = Request.ContentType,
        Headers = Request.Headers.ToDictionary(h => h.Key, h => h.Value),
    }, cancellationToken);

    return result is PaymentWebhookRejected ? BadRequest() : Ok();
}
order.status Result COMPLETED PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Finished CANCELED, REJECTED PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Rejected anything else / absent PaymentWebhookIgnored (status Processing)

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• Orders are created through the named HTTP client PayU.Orders (PayUServiceCaller.OrdersClientName), the other calls through PayU. RegisterPayUProvider() configures PayU.Orders not to follow redirects and without cookies: PayU answers an order with a 302 and the order id is in the body of that answer. If you configure the client yourself, keep AllowAutoRedirect = false - otherwise the provider throws InvalidOperationException rather than lose the id.
  • The default ServiceUrl is the PayU sandbox (https://secure.snd.payu.com) - set the production address explicitly.
  • Every order is sent with customerIp = 127.0.0.1; the payer's address is not forwarded to PayU.
  • Empty SignatureKey or no signature= in the OpenPayU-Signature header → PaymentWebhookRejected (InvalidSignature), fail-closed; constant-time comparison.
  • Supported algorithms: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 (matching the POS setting in the PayU panel); other algorithm= values are rejected. SHA-256 is recommended.
  • The webhook result carries PaymentUniqueId (order.orderId).

The methods a session actually offers are the ones described under configuration: p24 is not in the default PLN set, and PaymentRequest.PaymentChannel does not select a method (it is stored in the session metadata).

docs.title: Payment flow
docs.text:
1. RegisterPayment → creates a Stripe Checkout Session
  2. The user is redirected to RedirectUrl (hosted Stripe page)
  3. After the payment Stripe calls the webhook with the checkout.session.completed / payment_intent.payment_failed events
  4. The provider processes the webhook and returns PaymentWebhookResult

docs.title: Gateway errors
docs.text:
The Stripe.net SDK reports every API error as StripeException. From 3.0 the provider turns it into the outcomes every provider reports (in 2.x StripeException reached the application):

Situation Outcome RegisterPayment: Stripe could not handle the call (5xx, 408, 429, no answer) PaymentGatewayException with the StripeException as InnerException - the session may or may not exist RegisterPayment: a 4xx answer (invalid parameters, a payment method not enabled, a wrong key) PaymentStatus = Rejected, Stripe's message in ResponseObject GetStatus: any error, a 404 included PaymentGatewayException - a failed query says nothing about the payment 
try
{
    var payment = await payments.RegisterPayment(new PaymentRequest("Stripe", 129.00m, "PLN") { Title = "Order 42" }, cancellationToken);
    if (payment.PaymentStatus == PaymentStatusEnum.Rejected)
        return UnprocessableEntity(payment.ResponseObject);   // Stripe refused
    return Redirect(payment.RedirectUrl!);
}
catch (HttpRequestException)   // PaymentGatewayException: the state of the payment is not known
{
    return StatusCode(StatusCodes.Status503ServiceUnavailable);
}

docs.title: Webhook
docs.text:
Stripe verifies the webhook through Stripe-Signature in the header. Access to the raw body of the HTTP request is required.

[HttpPost("webhooks/stripe")]
public async Task<IActionResult> StripeWebhook(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    // The signature covers the exact bytes of the body - read it raw, not through [FromBody].
    using var reader = new StreamReader(Request.Body, Encoding.UTF8);
    var body = await reader.ReadToEndAsync(cancellationToken);

    var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync("Stripe", new PaymentWebhookRequest
    {
        Body = body,
        ContentType = Request.ContentType,
        Headers = Request.Headers.ToDictionary(h => h.Key, h => h.Value),
    }, cancellationToken);

    return result is PaymentWebhookRejected ? BadRequest() : Ok();
}
Event Result checkout.session.completed with payment_status = paid, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Finished, session id checkout.session.async_payment_failed, checkout.session.expired PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Rejected, session id payment_intent.succeeded / payment_intent.payment_failed PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Finished / Rejected, payment intent id checkout.session.completed not yet paid, another event, an event without an identifier PaymentWebhookIgnored

Raw body

Verifying the Stripe signature requires the raw request body. Do not use [FromBody] with automatic JSON deserialization — read Request.Body directly instead.

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• A missing WebhookSecret or Stripe-Signature header, or a signature that does not match, yields PaymentWebhookRejected (InvalidSignature) - Stripe.net is no longer invoked with an empty key.
  • checkout.session.expired, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/failed and payment_intent.succeeded/payment_failed carry PaymentUniqueId (session or payment-intent id).
  • The payment_intent.* events carry the payment intent id, not the session id returned by RegisterPayment. To match webhooks with stored session ids, act on the checkout.session.* events.

docs.text: The provider returns a fixed list for every currency: blik (BLIK), card (payment card), bank (online transfer).

docs.text: The provider obtains an OAuth2 token through the /oauth/auth endpoint for every RegisterPayment and GetStatus call. The token is not cached.

docs.title: Webhook
docs.text:
Tpay sends a transaction notification as a POST with an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body (fields id, tr_id, tr_amount, tr_crc, tr_status, md5sum, …). The provider accepts it only after two checks:

  1. md5sum = md5(id + tr_id + tr_amount + tr_crc + SecurityCode) - proves the notification is addressed to this merchant.
  2. The X-JWS-Signature header - an RS256 signature over the exact bytes of the body. The signing certificate is downloaded from the x5u address in the JWS header (it must point at JwsCertificateBaseUrl) and must chain to the Tpay root certificate (/x509/tpay-jws-root.pem).
[HttpPost("webhooks/tpay")]
public async Task<IActionResult> TpayWebhook(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    // The signature covers the exact bytes of the body - read it raw, not through [FromForm].
    using var reader = new StreamReader(Request.Body, Encoding.UTF8);
    var body = await reader.ReadToEndAsync(cancellationToken);

    var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync("Tpay", new PaymentWebhookRequest
    {
        Body = body,
        ContentType = Request.ContentType,
        Headers = Request.Headers.ToDictionary(h => h.Key, h => h.Value),
    }, cancellationToken);

    // Tpay repeats the notification until it gets a 200 response with the body "TRUE".
    return result is PaymentWebhookRejected
        ? BadRequest("FALSE")
        : Content(TpayProvider.Acknowledgement, "text/plain");
}
tr_status Result TRUE, PAID PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Finished CHARGEBACK, FALSE PaymentWebhookProcessed, status Rejected anything else / absent PaymentWebhookIgnored (status Processing)

PaymentUniqueId in the result is tr_crc, or tr_id (the Tpay transaction title, TR-…) when tr_crc is empty. The identifier returned by RequestPayment is not part of the notification, so pass your own order number in PaymentRequest.AdditionalData: the provider sends it as hiddenDescription and Tpay returns it in tr_crc.

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• Verification fails closed: an empty SecurityCode, a missing or wrong md5sum, a missing or malformed X-JWS-Signature, an algorithm other than RS256, a certificate outside the Tpay chain or past its validity → PaymentWebhookRejection.InvalidSignature.
  • md5sum is checked before any certificate is downloaded, so a request made without the SecurityCode causes no outgoing traffic.
  • The x5u address must have the same scheme, host and port as JwsCertificateBaseUrl (the whole origin is compared, not a text prefix - https://secure.tpay.com.example.net is refused).
  • tpay-jws-root.pem is a bundle: the CA that issues the signing certificate and the self-signed root. Only the self-signed certificate is a trust anchor; the machine certificate store is not used. JwsRootCertificatePem pins that bundle in configuration.
  • Certificates are kept in memory for an hour (ITpayServiceCaller is a singleton). When a signature does not match a cached certificate, the certificates are fetched again once - a certificate replaced by Tpay does not interrupt processing.
  • The sandbox signs with a different CA: set JwsCertificateBaseUrl to https://secure.sandbox.tpay.com.
  • JwsCertificateBaseUrl (an absolute https address) and JwsRootCertificatePem are validated when the host starts.
  • Breaking change (2.0): ITpayServiceCaller.VerifyNotification(body, signature) was replaced by VerifyNotificationAsync(body, jwsSignature, cancellationToken); the X-Signature header is no longer read.
  • What was verified: the chain against the certificates Tpay publishes (production and sandbox), the JWS signature and md5sum with tests that use their own certificate chain. Make a test payment in the Tpay sandbox before going live.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This library provides a set of base classes and interfaces for building paged and sorted queries in .NET applications. It standardizes the structure of list queries across the entire application — instead of passing page, pageSize, sortField as separate parameters everywhere, you have one consistent contract.

Key types: - QueryBase — abstract base class for query filter objects - PagedAndSortedQuery<TQuery> — base class combining filtering, pagination, and sorting - IPagedResult<T> — result contract with pagination: collection + total count - SortDirection — Asc/Desc/Undefined enum

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.Querying

docs.title: Defining the filter and the query
docs.text:
using TailoredApps.Shared.Querying;

// 1. Filter — the specific search criteria
public class CustomerFilter : QueryBase
{
    public string NameContains { get; set; }
    public string Email { get; set; }
    public bool? IsActive { get; set; }
    public DateTime? RegisteredAfter { get; set; }
}

// 2. Paged + sorted query
public class GetCustomersQuery : PagedAndSortedQuery<CustomerFilter>
{
    // All parameters are inherited:
    // Page, Count, SortField, SortDir, Filter, IsPagingSpecified, IsSortingSpecified
}

// 3. Paged result
public class CustomerListResult : IPagedResult<CustomerDto>
{
    public ICollection<CustomerDto> Results { get; set; }
    public int Count { get; set; }  // total count (without paging)
}

docs.title: Implementation in a repository / service
docs.text:
public async Task<CustomerListResult> GetCustomersAsync(
    GetCustomersQuery query,
    CancellationToken ct = default)
{
    var dbQuery = _context.Customers.AsQueryable();

    // Filters
    if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(query.Filter?.NameContains))
        dbQuery = dbQuery.Where(c => c.Name.Contains(query.Filter.NameContains));

    if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(query.Filter?.Email))
        dbQuery = dbQuery.Where(c => c.Email == query.Filter.Email);

    if (query.Filter?.IsActive.HasValue == true)
        dbQuery = dbQuery.Where(c => c.IsActive == query.Filter.IsActive.Value);

    // Sorting
    if (query.IsSortingSpecified)
    {
        // Example with IsSortBy()
        if (query.IsSortBy("Name"))
            dbQuery = query.SortDir == SortDirection.Asc
                ? dbQuery.OrderBy(c => c.Name)
                : dbQuery.OrderByDescending(c => c.Name);
        else if (query.IsSortBy("RegisteredAt"))
            dbQuery = query.SortDir == SortDirection.Asc
                ? dbQuery.OrderBy(c => c.RegisteredAt)
                : dbQuery.OrderByDescending(c => c.RegisteredAt);
    }

    var totalCount = await dbQuery.CountAsync(ct);

    // Paging
    if (query.IsPagingSpecified)
    {
        var skip = (query.Page!.Value - 1) * query.Count!.Value;
        dbQuery = dbQuery.Skip(skip).Take(query.Count.Value);
    }

    var items = await dbQuery
        .Select(c => new CustomerDto { Id = c.Id, Name = c.Name, Email = c.Email })
        .ToListAsync(ct);

    return new CustomerListResult
    {
        Results = items,
        Count = totalCount
    };
}

## TailoredApps.Shared.Querying - instructions for an AI agent

You are using TailoredApps.Shared.Querying to standardize paged queries.

### Type definitions
```csharp
// The filter inherits from QueryBase
public class MyFilter : QueryBase { public string Name { get; set; } }

// The query inherits from PagedAndSortedQuery<TFilter>
public class GetItemsQuery : PagedAndSortedQuery<MyFilter> { }

// The result implements IPagedResult<TItem>
public class ItemsResult : IPagedResult<ItemDto>
{
    public ICollection<ItemDto> Results { get; set; }
    public int Count { get; set; }
}
```

### URL parameters → automatic binding in ASP.NET Core
?page=1&count=20&sortField=Name&sortDir=Asc&filter.name=test

### In the service/repository
```csharp
if (query.IsPagingSpecified)
    dbQuery = dbQuery.Skip((query.Page!.Value - 1) * query.Count!.Value).Take(query.Count.Value);

if (query.IsSortingSpecified)
{
    if (query.IsSortBy("Name"))
        dbQuery = query.SortDir == SortDirection.Asc ? dbQuery.OrderBy(x => x.Name) : dbQuery.OrderByDescending(x => x.Name);
}
```

### Rules
- Count in IPagedResult = the total count without paging (for calculating pages in the UI)
- No sorting = SortDir is null (the default). SortDirection.Undefined is only the enum's zero value: IsSortingSpecified is still true for it when SortField is set, so handle it explicitly
- IsSortBy() compares case-insensitively — always use it instead of a manual string.Equals
- IsPagingSpecified = BOTH values, Page and Count, must be != null

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Production-ready defaults for ASP.NET Core Web APIs — a single call wires up the cross-cutting concerns every modern API needs, so each service starts with the same consistent observability, health-probing and resilient HTTP client configuration.

AddTailoredWebApiDefaults configures:

  • Metrics, tracing and logging — OpenTelemetry for ASP.NET Core, HttpClient and the .NET runtime, exported over OTLP
  • Health checks — readiness (/health, all checks) and liveness (/alive, checks tagged live)
  • HTTP clients — the standard resilience handler (retry, circuit breaker, timeouts) and service discovery on every factory-created client

Every feature binds from the WebApiDefaults configuration section and can be toggled independently. OTLP is the default exporter (stable); a ConfigureMetrics hook is provided for opting into a Prometheus scrape endpoint.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: dotnet add package TailoredApps.Shared.WebApi

docs.title: DI Registration
docs.text:
// Program.cs
using TailoredApps.Shared.WebApi;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Registers OpenTelemetry, health checks and resilient HTTP clients
builder.AddTailoredWebApiDefaults();

var app = builder.Build();

// Maps the /health (readiness) and /alive (liveness) endpoints
app.MapTailoredWebApiDefaults();

app.Run();

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Everything can be driven from the WebApiDefaults section in appsettings.json:

{
  "WebApiDefaults": {
    "ServiceName": "catalog-api",
    "ServiceVersion": "1.4.0",
    "HealthChecks": {
      "ReadinessPath": "/health",
      "LivenessPath": "/alive",
      "AllowDetailedResponse": false
    },
    "Observability": {
      "EnableMetrics": true,
      "EnableTracing": true,
      "EnableLogging": true,
      "OtlpExporterEndpoint": "http://otel-collector:4317"
    },
    "HttpClient": {
      "EnableStandardResilience": true,
      "EnableServiceDiscovery": true
    }
  }
}

The OTLP endpoint also honours the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT environment variable. When no endpoint is resolved, telemetry is still collected in-process but not exported anywhere.

Code overrides take precedence over configuration:

builder.AddTailoredWebApiDefaults(options =>
{
    options.ServiceName = "catalog-api";
    options.HealthChecks.AllowDetailedResponse = builder.Environment.IsDevelopment();
});

docs.title: Kubernetes probes
docs.text:
Once the endpoints are mapped, point your probes at them:

livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /alive
    port: 8080
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
    port: 8080

docs.title: Prometheus /metrics endpoint (optional)
docs.text:
Metrics flow over OTLP by default. If you need a local Prometheus-scrapable endpoint, add the OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Prometheus.AspNetCore package and use the hook:

builder.AddTailoredWebApiDefaults(options =>
{
    options.Observability.ConfigureMetrics = metrics => metrics.AddPrometheusExporter();
});

var app = builder.Build();
app.MapTailoredWebApiDefaults();
app.MapPrometheusScrapingEndpoint(); // /metrics

docs.title: 🔒 Security
docs.text:
• Retries only for safe methods. The standard resilience handler (AddStandardResilienceHandler) retries every request by default. A retried POST /charge whose first attempt reached the server is a duplicate charge. Retrying the methods that change state — POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, CONNECT — is therefore disabled (HttpClientSettings.RetryUnsafeHttpMethods = false); GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE are retried. Version 1.x still retried PUT and DELETE; from 2.0 the library uses the built-in DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods() of Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience. Enable retries only when every HTTP client in the host uses idempotency keys.
{ "WebApiDefaults": { "HttpClient": { "EnableStandardResilience": true, "RetryUnsafeHttpMethods": false } } }
