docs.title: Upgrading to 2.0
docs.text:
This page collects what has to be done in application code when moving from 1.x to 2.0. New capabilities are described on the pages of the individual libraries; here are only the changes after which code no longer compiles or behaves differently.

Requirements

The 2.0 libraries are released for net10.0 and net11.0. Applications on older platforms stay on the 1.6.x packages (security fixes). Details: Target frameworks.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text: # Library What to do If skipped 1 Payments Catch HttpRequestException around RegisterPayment and GetStatus A failing gateway ends the request with a 500 2 Payments Set PaymentProvider, Amount and Currency on every PaymentRequest Compile error CS9035 3 Payments (Tpay, Adyen) Pass the raw webhook body, answer with the text the gateway expects, send your own order number Notifications are rejected or repeated; a webhook cannot be matched with an order 4 Payments Handle the webhook result as one of three records - (the old properties still work) 5 MediatR Remove the ICache registration, clear the shared cache Compile error; entries in the old format are read 6 DateTime Nothing - optionally AddDateTimeProvider() and OffsetUtcNow -

docs.title: 1. A failing gateway is an exception, not the Rejected status
docs.text:
In 1.x a gateway that answered 5xx, or refused a status query, was reported as PaymentStatusEnum.Rejected. An application acting on that status cancelled an order whose payment may have succeeded.

In 2.0 Rejected means only what the gateway said. When the gateway gives no usable answer, the call throws PaymentGatewayException (derives from HttpRequestException) - the state of the payment is then not known.

// 1.x
var payment = await _payments.GetStatus("Tpay", paymentId);
if (payment.PaymentStatus == PaymentStatusEnum.Rejected)
    await _orders.CancelAsync(orderId);          // also when the gateway was failing!

// 2.0
try
{
    var payment = await _payments.GetStatus("Tpay", paymentId, cancellationToken);
    if (payment.PaymentStatus == PaymentStatusEnum.Rejected)
        await _orders.CancelAsync(orderId, cancellationToken);   // the gateway answered: declined
}
catch (HttpRequestException exception)   // covers PaymentGatewayException
{
    // The state of the payment is not known: leave the order as it is and check again later.
    _logger.LogWarning(exception, "Gateway unavailable for payment {PaymentId}", paymentId);
}

The same applies to RegisterPayment: a 5xx, 408 or 429 while creating a payment throws, because the payment may or may not have been created. A 4xx answer is still Rejected with the gateway's error text in ResponseObject.

  • PaymentGatewayException has Provider, StatusCode, IsTransient (whether a retry makes sense) and ResponseBody.
  • A timeout surfaces as TaskCanceledException.
  • Stripe reports failures as StripeException, as in 1.x (from 3.0 PaymentGatewayException too - see Upgrading to 3.0). CashBill still throws WebException in 2.0.0 and 2.0.1; from the next version PaymentGatewayException.

The full table of cases: Payments - A failing gateway is not a refusal.

docs.title: 2. PaymentRequest requires a provider, an amount and a currency
docs.text:
PaymentProvider, Amount and Currency are required members. An initializer that leaves one out does not compile (CS9035), and System.Text.Json refuses a document without them - an endpoint that takes a PaymentRequest from the body answers 400.

// 1.x - compiled, the error surfaced only at the gateway
var request = new PaymentRequest { Title = "Order 7", Amount = 49.99m };

// 2.0
var request = new PaymentRequest
{
    PaymentProvider = "Tpay",
    Amount = 49.99m,
    Currency = "PLN",
    Title = "Order 7",
};

// or shorter
var request = new PaymentRequest("Tpay", 49.99m, "PLN") { Title = "Order 7" };

RegisterPayment also refuses a blank provider key or currency (ArgumentException) and an amount of zero or less (ArgumentOutOfRangeException) before it calls the gateway.

docs.title: 3. Tpay and Adyen webhooks
docs.text:
In 1.x the verification of both gateways' notifications did not match their protocols and rejected genuine notifications. In 2.0 it works, but needs three things from the application.

a) Pass the raw body. The signature covers the exact bytes of the request. Read the body from the stream - not through [FromForm], [FromBody] or a re-serialization.

b) Answer with the text the gateway expects. It is in PaymentResponse.ResponseObject of the result and in the constants TpayProvider.Acknowledgement (TRUE) and AdyenProvider.Acknowledgement ([accepted]). Any other answer makes the gateway repeat the notification.

c) Send your own order number in PaymentRequest.AdditionalData. Tpay and Adyen notifications do not carry the identifier returned by RegisterPayment. PaymentUniqueId of the webhook result is the value from AdditionalData (Tpay: tr_crc, Adyen: merchantReference); without it you get only the gateway's reference, which the application does not know.

[HttpPost("webhooks/tpay")]
public async Task<IActionResult> TpayWebhook(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    using var reader = new StreamReader(Request.Body, Encoding.UTF8);
    var body = await reader.ReadToEndAsync(cancellationToken);                 // a) the raw body

    var result = await _payments.HandleWebhookAsync("Tpay", new PaymentWebhookRequest
    {
        Body = body,
        ContentType = Request.ContentType,
        Headers = Request.Headers.ToDictionary(h => h.Key, h => h.Value),
    }, cancellationToken);

    if (result is PaymentWebhookProcessed processed)
        await _orders.ApplyPaymentAsync(processed.Payment.PaymentUniqueId, processed.Payment.PaymentStatus, cancellationToken);   // c) the order number

    return result is PaymentWebhookRejected
        ? BadRequest("FALSE")
        : Content(TpayProvider.Acknowledgement, "text/plain");                 // b) "TRUE"
}

In addition:

  • Tpay: the signature header is X-JWS-Signature (not X-Signature); in the sandbox set JwsCertificateBaseUrl to https://secure.sandbox.tpay.com. Your own ITpayServiceCaller implementation needs VerifyNotificationAsync instead of VerifyNotification.
  • Adyen: the signature is in additionalData.hmacSignature of the notification item, not in a header. Enable HMAC signing of the webhook in the Adyen Customer Area and copy the key into NotificationHmacKey.

Details and status tables: Tpay, Adyen.

docs.title: 4. Other changes in Payments
docs.text:
• The webhook result is one of three records: PaymentWebhookProcessed, PaymentWebhookIgnored, PaymentWebhookRejected (with the reason in Rejection). The former Success, Ignored and ErrorMessage still work.
  • CancellationToken is an optional parameter of every asynchronous method. Calls need no change; your own provider (IPaymentProvider, I*ServiceCaller) has to add the parameter to the methods it implements.
  • Configuration is validated at startup: Register*Provider() stops the host (OptionsValidationException) when credentials or the webhook secret are missing. Register only the providers you have configured.

Described on: Payments.

docs.title: MediatR
docs.text:
CachingBehavior uses HybridCache. The ICache interface and the Cache class are removed together with the Newtonsoft.Json dependency:

  • delete your own ICache registration,
  • ICachePolicy.SlidingExpiration is no longer supported,
  • after upgrading, clear the shared cache or change the key prefix - entries written by 1.x have a different format.

Retries and the circuit breaker no longer use Polly. Described on: MediatR.

docs.title: DateTime
docs.text:
Code that uses IDateTimeProvider needs no change; your own implementations of the interface and existing mocks compile as before.

  • DateTimeProvider reads its time from System.TimeProvider, so an application has one clock.
  • New: OffsetUtcNow and OffsetNow (DateTimeOffset) and the registration builder.Services.AddDateTimeProvider().
  • UtcTimeOfDaty (a typo) is obsolete - use UtcTimeOfDay (removed in 3.0).
  • Behaviour change: Now and Today report the time zone of the TimeProvider in use (no difference for the system clock).

Described on: DateTime.

docs.title: Other libraries
docs.text:
• All: the public API carries nullable annotations - a project with <Nullable>enable</Nullable> may see new warnings (Target frameworks).
  • EntityFramework: PagingAsync works for non-empty pages (in 1.x it threw InvalidOperationException).
  • WebApi: the default HTTP client resilience does not retry requests that change state (WebApi).

docs.title: 🤖 AI Agent Prompt
docs.text:
## Upgrading TailoredApps.Shared.* from 1.x to 2.0 - instructions for an AI agent

You are upgrading a .NET 10 or .NET 11 application from the TailoredApps.Shared.* 1.x packages to 2.0. Do the following in order:

### Registration
- Raise every TailoredApps.Shared.* package to the same 2.x version
- Remove the ICache registration (MediatR); optionally add builder.Services.AddDateTimeProvider()

### What needs code changes
- Payments: wrap every IPaymentService.RegisterPayment and GetStatus call in try/catch (HttpRequestException) - a failing gateway is an unknown state, not a refusal
- Payments: every new PaymentRequest must set PaymentProvider, Amount (> 0) and Currency
- Payments: webhook endpoints pass the raw body from the request stream and every header
- Tpay: HTTP 200 with the body "TRUE" (TpayProvider.Acknowledgement); Adyen: "[accepted]" (AdyenProvider.Acknowledgement)
- Tpay and Adyen: set PaymentRequest.AdditionalData to the order number; in the webhook match the order by PaymentUniqueId
- Your own IPaymentProvider / I*ServiceCaller implementations: add the parameter CancellationToken cancellationToken = default

### Configuration
- Tpay sandbox: Payments:Providers:Tpay:JwsCertificateBaseUrl = "https://secure.sandbox.tpay.com"
- Adyen: Payments:Providers:Adyen:NotificationHmacKey = the webhook HMAC key (hex) from the Adyen Customer Area
- Every registered provider needs its full credentials and webhook secret, otherwise the host does not start

### Rules
- Do not cancel an order after an exception from RegisterPayment / GetStatus; Rejected is reliable only when the call returned a result
- Do not read a webhook body through [FromForm] or [FromBody] - the signature covers the raw bytes
- Do not replace signature verification with a stub that returns true
- After upgrading MediatR clear the shared cache or change the key prefix
- Applications on net8.0 / net9.0 / netstandard stay on 1.6.x - do not raise them to 2.0

docs.title: Upgrading to 3.0 (test phase)
docs.text:
Test phase

The 3.0 line is released as pre-releases (3.0.0-preview.N). The API may still change before 3.0.0. Production applications stay on 2.1.x (branch release/2.1, fixes) until 3.0 leaves the test phase.

This page collects what has to be done in application code when moving from 2.x to 3.0.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text:
The TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR* libraries no longer depend on the MediatR package and use ForkForward.Mediator - a community fork of MediatR 12.5.0, the last version under the Apache-2.0 licence (MediatR is commercially licensed from version 13). The fork has the same types, members and behaviour, but its own namespace and assembly: ForkForward.Mediator instead of MediatR.

The package names and namespaces of these libraries (TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR, TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.Caching, …) do not change.

docs.title: Stripe reports gateway errors the way the other providers do
docs.text:
In 2.x the Stripe provider let every API error through as the StripeException of the Stripe.net SDK. From 3.0 it follows the same rules as the other eight providers:

Situation 2.x 3.0 RegisterPayment: Stripe could not handle the call (5xx, 408, 429, no answer) StripeException PaymentGatewayException (an HttpRequestException), with the StripeException as InnerException RegisterPayment: Stripe refused it (4xx - invalid parameters, a payment method not enabled, a wrong key) StripeException PaymentStatus = Rejected, Stripe's message in ResponseObject GetStatus: any error, a 404 included StripeException PaymentGatewayException

An application that already catches HttpRequestException around RegisterPayment and GetStatus (recommended since 2.0) now handles Stripe with the same block. Stripe webhook handling does not change.

docs.title: Refused requests are no longer logged as errors
docs.text:
• MediatR - LoggingBehavior logs a request refused by validation (ValidationException) at Information level: Request GetProduct rejected by validation …; invalid: Id, with the property names only (validation messages can quote the values the client sent). A request cancelled by its caller (OperationCanceledException while the request's token is cancelled) is Information too. Every other handler exception is Error, as before.
  • ExceptionHandling - ConfigureExceptionHandler() no longer treats an exception the provider answers with a 4xx status as an error: the middleware does not write An unhandled exception has occurred while executing the request. at Error level and does not add the error.type tag to the http.server.request.duration metric. The exception is logged at Debug level, in the TailoredApps.Shared.ExceptionHandling category. 5xx answers do not change.

Before, one validation failure produced two Error entries with stack traces.

docs.title: Removed obsolete members
docs.text:
The members marked [Obsolete] in 2.x are gone. The 2.x compiler warned about every use of them (CS0618).

Removed Use instead After the upgrade, unchanged code IDateTimeProvider.UtcTimeOfDaty, DateTimeProvider.UtcTimeOfDaty (typo) UtcTimeOfDay Compile error (CS1061) FilterCollection.AddExceptionHAndlingFilterAttribute() (typo) AddExceptionHandlingFilterAttribute() Compile error (CS1061) PayNowServiceOptions.ApiUrl, the Payments:Providers:PayNow:ApiUrl key ServiceUrl Code: compile error. Configuration: the host does not start, with 'Payments:Providers:PayNow:ApiUrl' is no longer read (removed in 3.0): rename it to 'ServiceUrl'. TpayServiceOptions.ApiUrl, the Payments:Providers:Tpay:ApiUrl key ServiceUrl as above, for Tpay

The old configuration key is detected on purpose: if it were only ignored, a sandbox setup (ApiUrl holding the sandbox address) would, after the upgrade, silently connect to the production default of ServiceUrl.

docs.title: New packages for minimal APIs
docs.text:
Two new packages of their own - they change nothing in the existing ones and nothing has to be migrated:

  • ExceptionHandling.MinimalApi - WithExceptionHandling() and WithValidation<TRequest>() as endpoint filters, with the same error model as the middleware and the MVC filter; NativeAOT-compatible.
  • EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.MinimalApi - WithUnitOfWorkTransaction(): commit after a success, rollback after an exception or a result with a status ≥ 400, the rules of the MVC filter.

docs.title: Trimming and NativeAOT
docs.text:
DateTime, Querying, Email, Email.Models, ExceptionHandling, WebApi, Payments and the eight HTTP providers (all but Stripe) declare in 3.0 that they are safe for trimming and NativeAOT (in a Web API: with minimal APIs, not controllers): options are bound by code generated at compile time and the gateways' JSON is serialized through generated metadata. Nothing changes for an application - request bodies and signatures are identical. Details and the list of libraries: Trimming and NativeAOT.

One behaviour change: CashbillHttpClient.MakeFormRequest<T>() reads answers only as types the library has JSON metadata for - the CashBill models (Payment, PaymentStatus, List<PaymentChannels>) and built-in types. For a type of your own it throws NotSupportedException before the request is sent.

Apart from that, the libraries have no change in 3.0 that requires code modifications.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text: # What to do If skipped 1 Remove the MediatR package (and MediatR.Contracts) from the application and add ForkForward.Mediator - or rely on the transitive dependency of TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR Two different sets of IRequest / IRequestHandler types; handlers are not found 2 Replace using MediatR; with using ForkForward.Mediator; (also MediatR.Pipeline → ForkForward.Mediator.Pipeline and so on) Compile errors (CS0246) or type mismatches 3 Replace AddMediatR(...) with AddMediator(...), and MediatRServiceConfiguration with MediatorServiceConfiguration Compile error (CS1061) 4 Raise every TailoredApps.Shared.* package to the same 3.0 version Mixing 2.x and 3.0 puts two mediators in one process 5 Stripe: handle an outage with catch (HttpRequestException) and a refusal with PaymentStatus == Rejected; remove catch (StripeException) around RegisterPayment and GetStatus A Stripe outage bypasses the old catch (StripeException) block, and a refusal is no longer an exception and goes unhandled 6 Review alerts and queries that count Error entries or error.type for 4xx answers An alert on "validation errors" stops firing 7 Replace UtcTimeOfDaty with UtcTimeOfDay, AddExceptionHAndlingFilterAttribute with AddExceptionHandlingFilterAttribute, and the ApiUrl key of the PayNow and Tpay configuration with ServiceUrl A compile error, or a host that does not start

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// 2.x
using MediatR;

builder.Services.AddMediatR(cfg => cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly));

var pipeline = new PipelineRegistration(builder.Services);
pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors();
pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors(typeof(Program).Assembly);

public record GetProduct(int Id) : IRequest<ProductDto>;

public class GetProductHandler : IRequestHandler<GetProduct, ProductDto>
{
    public Task<ProductDto> Handle(GetProduct request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) => /* … */;
}

// 3.0
using ForkForward.Mediator;

builder.Services.AddMediator(cfg => cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly));

var pipeline = new PipelineRegistration(builder.Services);     // the TailoredApps registration - unchanged
pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors();
pipeline.RegisterPipelineBehaviors(typeof(Program).Assembly);

public record GetProduct(int Id) : IRequest<ProductDto>;

public class GetProductHandler : IRequestHandler<GetProduct, ProductDto>
{
    public Task<ProductDto> Handle(GetProduct request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) => /* … */;
}

Only the using directive and the name of the method that registers the mediator change. IRequest<>, IRequestHandler<,>, IPipelineBehavior<,>, IMediator, ISender, INotification and the other types keep their names and members.

In a large project two replacements across the solution are enough: using MediatR → using ForkForward.Mediator and AddMediatR( → AddMediator(.

A working example on ForkForward.Mediator - the whole pipeline (validation, caching, retry, fallback) together with the other libraries - is the demo application.

docs.title: Things to watch
docs.text:
• Do not mix the two mediators. A handler that implements MediatR.IRequestHandler<,> is not called by ForkForward.Mediator.IMediator and the other way round - they are different types. After the migration no reference to the MediatR package should remain in the application.
  • Third-party libraries built on MediatR (your own packages with handlers, for example) have to be rebuilt on ForkForward.Mediator before they work with 3.0.
  • The behaviour is that of MediatR 12.5.0 - the order of behaviours, notification publishing and registration from an assembly work the same way.
  • ForkForward.Mediator is a young package. That is why 3.0 is in a test phase: try it in one application before moving the others.
  • The details of a Stripe error (StripeError.Code, Type) are still there: for an outage in PaymentGatewayException.InnerException (the StripeException); for a refusal Stripe's message is in PaymentResponse.ResponseObject.
  • Your own types in CashbillHttpClient.MakeFormRequest<T>() are no longer supported (NotSupportedException) - read the answer as a JsonElement or use an HTTP client of your own.
  • An exception the provider answers with a 4xx no longer shows in the log at Error level. If the application maps exceptions that are really server errors to 4xx, have the provider give them a 5xx.

The libraries: MediatR. Upgrading from 1.x: Upgrading to 2.0.

docs.title: 🤖 AI Agent Prompt
docs.text:
## Upgrading TailoredApps.Shared.* from 2.x to 3.0 (preview) - instructions for an AI agent

You are upgrading a .NET 10 or .NET 11 application from the TailoredApps.Shared.* 2.x packages to 3.0.0-preview. The changes that need code modifications: the mediator, Stripe error handling and the removed obsolete members.

### Registration
- Raise every TailoredApps.Shared.* package to the same 3.0.0-preview.N version
- Remove references to the MediatR and MediatR.Contracts packages; add ForkForward.Mediator where needed
- Replace builder.Services.AddMediatR(...) with builder.Services.AddMediator(...)

### What needs code changes
- using MediatR; -> using ForkForward.Mediator; (and MediatR.Pipeline -> ForkForward.Mediator.Pipeline and so on)
- MediatRServiceConfiguration -> MediatorServiceConfiguration
- The names and members of IRequest, IRequestHandler, IPipelineBehavior, IMediator, ISender, INotification do not change
- Stripe: replace catch (StripeException) around RegisterPayment/GetStatus with catch (HttpRequestException) (outage) and a check of PaymentStatus == Rejected (refusal)
- Alerts that count Error entries for validation failures stop working: validation is logged at Information level
- UtcTimeOfDaty -> UtcTimeOfDay; AddExceptionHAndlingFilterAttribute -> AddExceptionHandlingFilterAttribute; in appsettings*.json, environment variables and secrets: Payments:Providers:PayNow:ApiUrl and Payments:Providers:Tpay:ApiUrl -> ServiceUrl (the old key stops the host from starting)

### Configuration
- No new configuration keys

### Rules
- After the migration no reference to the MediatR package or namespace may remain in the solution
- Do not rename the TailoredApps.Shared.MediatR.* namespaces - they are library names, not the MediatR package
- Do not mix TailoredApps.Shared.* packages of versions 2.x and 3.0 in one application
- 3.0 is a pre-release: do not deploy it to production without an explicit decision of the application owner

docs.title: Target frameworks, runtime async and NativeAOT
docs.text: Every TailoredApps.Shared.* package is built for several target frameworks at once (multi-targeting). NuGet picks the asset that matches your application's TargetFramework — there is nothing to configure.

docs.title: Supported target frameworks
docs.text:
Libraries Target frameworks DateTime, Email, Email.Models, Email.Office365, EntityFramework, EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.MinimalApi, EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.WebApiCore, ExceptionHandling, ExceptionHandling.MinimalApi, MediatR, MediatR.Caching, MediatR.Email, MediatR.ML, MediatR.PagedRequest, Payments and every payment provider, Querying, WebApi net10.0, net11.0

Version 2.0 and older frameworks

From version 2.0 every library targets net10.0 and net11.0 only. Applications on net8.0, net9.0, .NET Framework or any other netstandard2.0 / netstandard2.1 platform stay on the 1.x packages (1.6.x), which keep receiving security fixes from the release/1.x branch.

docs.title: Framework-aligned dependencies
docs.text:
Packages tied to the runtime generation (Microsoft.Extensions.*, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore*) have a separate version for each target framework: the net11.0 asset depends on the 11.x line and net10.0 on 10.x. Every package version is recorded in one place, Directory.Packages.props; project files name packages without a version. An application on .NET 11 therefore does not pull in packages from the previous generation.

Exception: WebApi on net11.0

On the day .NET 11 was released, nuget.org had no 11.x line of Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience and Microsoft.Extensions.ServiceDiscovery yet, so the net11.0 asset of WebApi temporarily uses their 10.x line.

docs.title: Runtime async (.NET 11)
docs.text:
In .NET 11 the runtime itself can suspend and resume async methods. The C# compiler then no longer generates a separate state machine type for every async method — the method stays an ordinary method marked with the MethodImplOptions.Async flag. The goal is lower overhead for asynchronous calls and smaller IL. Source code and public API are unchanged: signatures still return Task / ValueTask.

The libraries in this repository use it in their net11.0 assets:

Asset in the package How async methods are compiled net11.0 runtime async net10.0 compiler-generated state machine (unchanged)

docs.title: What it means for your application
docs.text:
• Nothing to switch on. An application on net11.0 gets the runtime-async asset automatically; applications on net10.0 get exactly what they got before.
  • Your application does not have to use runtime async itself. Classically compiled code can freely call library methods compiled as runtime async and the other way round — this repository's tests are compiled classically and run on both net10.0 and net11.0.
  • No environment variables and no <EnablePreviewFeatures> are needed.

Requires CoreCLR or NativeAOT

Runtime async works on CoreCLR and NativeAOT. The Mono runtime — used by Blazor WebAssembly, among others — cannot execute such methods in .NET 11. If you want to use one of the libraries that contain async code on the Blazor WebAssembly client side on net11.0, build it with runtime async switched off (see below). DateTime, Email.Models, MediatR.Caching and Querying contain no async code and are not affected.

Feature status

In .NET 11 runtime async is an opt-in feature that Microsoft's documentation still describes as a preview: What's new in the .NET 11 runtime.

docs.title: How it is enabled in the repository
docs.text:
One place: eng/RuntimeAsync.targets, imported by src/Directory.Build.targets (every library) and samples/Directory.Build.targets (the demo application). The file appends runtime-async=on to the compiler's Features property only for target frameworks compatible with net11.0:

<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(UseRuntimeAsync)' != 'false' and '$(TargetFramework)' != '' and $([MSBuild]::IsTargetFrameworkCompatible('$(TargetFramework)', 'net11.0'))">
  <Features>$(Features);runtime-async=on</Features>
</PropertyGroup>

The condition is required: setting the flag for net10.0 fails the build with SYSLIB5007 / CA2252, and on older frameworks the flag is silently ignored.

The test projects are compiled the classic way on purpose, so on net11.0 every test crosses from state-machine code into runtime-async code and back. The RuntimeAsyncTests test checks with reflection that the net11.0 assets of the libraries and the demo hold no state machines and the net10.0 assets no runtime-async methods - if the flag stopped reaching the compiler, nothing else would notice. Runtime async under NativeAOT is checked by the smoke application described in Trimming and NativeAOT.

docs.title: Switching it off
docs.text:
Scope How Whole build dotnet build TailoredApps.Shared.slnx -p:UseRuntimeAsync=false One library or application <UseRuntimeAsync>false</UseRuntimeAsync> in its .csproj file

With the switch off, the net11.0 asset is compiled like the others — with state machines.

docs.title: Trimming and NativeAOT
docs.text:
From version 3.0 some of the libraries declare that they are safe for trimming and NativeAOT (IsAotCompatible). An application published with <PublishAot>true</PublishAot> or <PublishTrimmed>true</PublishTrimmed> gets no IL2xxx / IL3xxx warnings from them, and their code works once compiled to native code.

Libraries State DateTime, Querying, Email.Models, Payments, Payments.Provider.Adyen, .CashBill, .HotPay, .PayNow, .PayU, .Przelewy24, .Revolut, .Tpay Compatible. Checked natively in CI on net10.0 and net11.0, on Linux and Windows Email, ExceptionHandling, ExceptionHandling.MinimalApi, WebApi Compatible in a minimal-API application (see below). The MVC filter of ExceptionHandling does not apply: ASP.NET Core does not support controllers under NativeAOT MediatR.Caching The library's own code raises no warnings, but it is only useful together with MediatR MediatR, MediatR.Email, MediatR.PagedRequest Not compatible: the mediator creates generic handler types at run time, registration scans assemblies, and the default cache key serializes the request with reflection EntityFramework, EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.WebApiCore, EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.MinimalApi Not compatible: EF Core builds its model and queries at run time; change auditing creates types with MakeGenericType Email.Office365, MediatR.ML, Payments.Provider.Stripe Not compatible: their dependencies (Microsoft.Identity.Web, ML.NET, Stripe.net) rely on reflection

docs.title: Web API: minimal APIs yes, controllers no
docs.text:
NativeAOT in ASP.NET Core covers minimal APIs, not MVC. Checked on .NET 11 in this repository:

Scenario Result after PublishAot Minimal API + WebApi + ExceptionHandling (middleware and endpoint filters with a FluentValidation validator) + Email + [Authorize] with a JWT (401 / 403 / 200) No warnings, works natively - this is what tests/TailoredApps.Shared.AotSmoke.Web does Controllers (AddControllers, [ApiController], [Authorize]) About 160 warnings from MVC alone; the application starts, but every controller route answers 404 - the controllers are not discovered Controllers + EF Core + the transaction filter Several hundred warnings from EF Core; the application dies at startup

Authorization is not the obstacle: [Authorize], policies and JWT work natively on minimal-API endpoints. Controllers and EF Core are. An application with controllers therefore keeps using the libraries as before (JIT, ReadyToRun if wanted), and NativeAOT requires its endpoints rewritten as minimal APIs and data access without EF Core.

Minimal APIs have packages of their own with the counterparts of the MVC filters: ExceptionHandling.MinimalApi (exceptions and validation, NativeAOT-compatible) and EntityFramework.UnitOfWork.MinimalApi (a transaction per request; works without AOT, because it depends on EF Core).

docs.title: Blazor
docs.text:
• Blazor Server / a Blazor Web App rendered on the server runs on the regular CoreCLR: the libraries work without restrictions and NativeAOT does not apply.
  • Blazor WebAssembly runs on the Mono runtime, which in .NET 11 does not execute runtime-async methods. Checked: calling an async method of a library from its net11.0 asset fails with PlatformNotSupportedException: Runtime Async is not supported on this platform. Code without async (DateTime, Querying, Email.Models, for example) works. Until packages with a separate asset for the browser are published, a WebAssembly application on net11.0 cannot use the async methods of these libraries; one on net10.0 gets the asset with state machines and works.
  • What matters in the browser is trimming (always on when publishing), not NativeAOT - the libraries in the "Compatible" rows raise no trimmer warnings.

docs.title: What was done
docs.text:
• Options from configuration are bound by code generated at compile time (the configuration binding generator), not by reflection. The exception is Email.Office365, where the generator cannot bind the certificate description.
  • The JSON of the payment gateways is serialized through metadata generated at compile time (JsonSerializerContext); request bodies and signatures are identical byte for byte. The same goes for the error response of ExceptionHandling.
  • Container registrations with a generic parameter (RegisterPaymentProvider<T>(), AddPayments<,>(), AddExceptionHandlingForWebApi<,>()) carry annotations that make the trimmer keep the constructors dependency injection calls.

docs.title: How it is kept that way
docs.text:
• In a library with <IsAotCompatible>true</IsAotCompatible> every warning of the trimming, AOT and single-file analyzers is a compile error (eng/AotCompatible.globalconfig, wired up in src/Directory.Build.targets).
  • tests/TailoredApps.Shared.AotSmoke is a console application that uses these libraries the way an application does: container, options from configuration, a payment at every HTTP gateway (through the same gateway fake as the demo application), notifications, signatures. tests/TailoredApps.Shared.AotSmoke.Web is a minimal-API Web API: it starts on a free port and calls its own endpoints - health, error responses, an e-mail template and SMTP, [Authorize] with a JWT, an HTTP client with resilience. The NativeAOT smoke test job of the PR checks publishes both with NativeAOT for net10.0 and net11.0, on Linux and Windows, and runs them; in those projects every trim/AOT warning - from dependencies too - is an error. The analyzers see the code of one library, the AOT compiler the whole dependency closure.
dotnet publish tests/TailoredApps.Shared.AotSmoke -c Release -f net11.0 -r linux-x64   # needs clang and zlib; on Windows: -r win-x64 and the C++ build tools
./artifacts/publish/TailoredApps.Shared.AotSmoke/release_net11.0_linux-x64/TailoredApps.Shared.AotSmoke

docs.title: Nullable reference types
docs.text:
From version 2.0 every library is compiled with nullable reference types enabled, so the public API tells the compiler which values may be null:

  • Members that were never guaranteed to hold a value are now declared nullable — for example PaymentRequest.Currency, PaymentResponse.RedirectUrl, MailMessage.Body or the optional properties of the option classes. If your project has <Nullable>enable</Nullable>, the compiler now warns where such a value is used without a check.
  • Parameters that always accepted null are declared that way — for example the attachments of IEmailProvider.SendMail.
  • Nothing changes at run time for code that already worked. The only differences are on paths that used to end in a NullReferenceException, which now fail with a descriptive exception — for instance a payment request without a currency throws ArgumentException, and auditing an entity without a primary key throws InvalidOperationException.

In the repository itself nullable warnings are build errors for everything under src/ (src/Directory.Build.props), so the annotations cannot drift from the code.

docs.title: Building the repository
docs.text:
• .NET SDK 11.0.100 or newer is required — it builds both target frameworks, net10.0 and net11.0.
  • The tests run on net10.0 and net11.0, so both runtimes are needed locally.
  • The CI workflows install the 10.0.x SDK (runtime for the net10.0 tests) and 11.0.x (build).
dotnet build TailoredApps.Shared.slnx
dotnet test TailoredApps.Shared.slnx

docs.title: Adding a new library
docs.text:
• Do not set TargetFrameworks, author, licence or language version in the .csproj — they are inherited from Directory.Build.props and src/Directory.Build.props. A project file holds only what is its own: PackageId, Title, Description, PackageTags, references.
  • Add packages as <PackageReference Include="Name" /> without a version; put the version in Directory.Packages.props. A runtime-aligned package goes into both conditional groups (10.* for net10.0, 11.* for net11.0).
  • Do not set Features in the .csproj — runtime async is inherited from eng/RuntimeAsync.targets.
  • If the library is to be NativeAOT-compatible: set <IsAotCompatible>true</IsAotCompatible>, add it to tests/TailoredApps.Shared.AotSmoke with a check of its scenario, and add it to the table in Trimming and NativeAOT.
  • Put the test project under tests/ — it inherits the same target frameworks, so the net11.0 asset is actually tested.

docs.title: 🤖 AI Agent Prompt
docs.text:
## TailoredApps Shared Components — target frameworks and runtime async — AI agent instructions

You are working with TailoredApps.Shared.* packages or with the SharedComponents repository.

### Registration
- None. Choosing a target framework needs no Program.cs calls — NuGet selects the asset that
  matches the application's TargetFramework.

### What gets configured
- Frameworks from version 2.0: net10.0 and net11.0 for every library. Older frameworks
  (net8.0, net9.0, netstandard2.x) are served only by the 1.x packages (1.6.x).
- The net11.0 assets have their async methods compiled as runtime async; every other asset uses
  compiler-generated state machines. The public API is identical on every framework.
- Microsoft.Extensions.* / EF Core dependencies are aligned with the framework (net11.0 -> 11.x).

### Configuration
- In the repository: the UseRuntimeAsync MSBuild property (on by default for net11.0+), handled
  in eng/RuntimeAsync.targets (the libraries and the demo application). Switch off with -p:UseRuntimeAsync=false or
  <UseRuntimeAsync>false</UseRuntimeAsync> in the library's csproj.
- In an application consuming the packages: no settings.

### Rules
- Do not add <Features>runtime-async=on</Features> or <EnablePreviewFeatures> to library csproj
  files — the switch is central and conditioned on the target framework.
- Do not set runtime-async for net10.0 or older frameworks: the build fails with
  SYSLIB5007 / CA2252.
- Do not use the net11.0 assets of libraries containing async code in Blazor WebAssembly (Mono
  does not support runtime async in .NET 11) — build them with UseRuntimeAsync=false.
- New library: do not set TargetFrameworks or package metadata in the csproj (they are inherited);
  PackageReference without a version, versions in Directory.Packages.props (runtime-aligned packages
  in both conditional groups: 10.* and 11.*); test project under tests/.
- Build the repository with .NET SDK 11.0.100 or newer.
- Safe for trimming and NativeAOT (IsAotCompatible): DateTime, Querying, Email, Email.Models, ExceptionHandling,
  ExceptionHandling.MinimalApi, WebApi,
  Payments and the providers Adyen, CashBill, HotPay, PayNow, PayU, Przelewy24, Revolut, Tpay.
- NativeAOT in ASP.NET Core means minimal APIs: MVC controllers do not work natively (their routes answer 404). [Authorize] and JWT do.
- Blazor WebAssembly on net11.0 does not execute runtime-async methods (PlatformNotSupportedException): do not call the async
  methods of the libraries from the net11.0 asset there. IL2xxx/IL3xxx warnings are compile errors there:
  no reflection, no JsonSerializer without a JsonTypeInfo, no ConfigurationBinder outside the generator.
- The MediatR*, EntityFramework*, Email.Office365, MediatR.ML and Payments.Provider.Stripe libraries are not
  NativeAOT-compatible - do not suggest them for an application published with PublishAot.

docs.title: Security review - September 2026
docs.text: This page records the security review of the shared libraries performed on 2 September 2026, the fixes that shipped with it, and the items that still need a human decision.

docs.title: Scope and method
docs.text:
• Every library under src/ (25 projects, about 12 000 lines of C#), the test projects, the GitHub Actions workflows and the PowerShell automation scripts.
  • Static review of all sources in five passes (payments core and providers, EF/Querying, MediatR/Email/ML, WebApi/ExceptionHandling, CI), each finding re-verified against the code before a fix was written.
  • dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive: no vulnerable NuGet packages (direct or transitive). System.Linq.Dynamic.Core is pinned above the CVE-2024-51417 fix.
  • Every fix is covered by unit tests; the whole solution (build + 900+ tests) was green before commit.

docs.title: Findings and status
docs.text: # Severity Area Finding Status 1 Critical Payments (tests) A production CashBill shop secret and matching signatures were committed in a test source file (unused test data). Removed from source. Rotation and history purge require the owner - see Action items. 2 High ExceptionHandling Default provider returned the innermost exception message (SQL errors, hosts, paths) to anonymous callers as HTTP 400 in every environment. Fixed: 500 + generic message; details only in Development or on explicit opt-in. 3 High Payments (all providers) Signature verification silently degraded to an unkeyed hash when the secret was missing, so anyone could forge a "valid" notification. Fixed: fail-closed in all 9 providers (incl. Stripe). 4 High Payments (CashBill) Webhook error message echoed the expected signature (an oracle for forging notifications); legacy TransactionStatusChange performed no verification. Fixed. 5 High Payments (Revolut) Signed payload used v1: instead of v1.; no timestamp check, so a captured webhook was replayable forever. Fixed: correct format, 300 s tolerance (configurable), multi-signature rotation. 6 High EntityFramework Client-controlled SortField passed straight to Dynamic LINQ (navigation traversal, multi-column, schema disclosure); no upper bound on page size. Fixed: identifier validation, allow-list overload, page bounds and overflow checks. 7 High MediatR Default cache key used ToString() on properties, so requests differing only in collection contents shared one entry (cross-user data). Logging scope serialized whole requests (secrets, images). Fixed: content-hash keys; scope carries only type name + correlation id. 8 High Email Template variables inserted verbatim into HTML bodies (phishing links from a trusted sender); comma-separated recipient strings added extra recipients; SMTP TLS off by default. Fixed: HTML-encoding by default ({{{raw}}} opt-out), single recipient, TLS on. 9 High MediatR.ML Training command read any directory and wrote any file path from the request; classification accepted unbounded, unvalidated bytes. Fixed: paths confined to TrainingRoot/ModelsRoot; size and signature validation. 10 Medium WebApi Standard resilience handler retried POST/PATCH on every HttpClient, duplicating payments/orders after timeouts. Fixed: unsafe-method retries disabled by default. 11 Medium Payments Non-constant-time signature comparison; case-sensitive header lookup (broken under HTTP/2); unescaped identifiers in gateway URLs; webhook results without a payment id. Fixed: WebhookSignature, case-insensitive dictionaries, PaymentIdentifier, ids populated. 12 Medium Payments (Przelewy24) Notification/verify signatures computed over the wrong field sets (every genuine notification rejected). Fixed to the documented field order. 13 Medium EF UnitOfWork Transaction filter committed when the action returned 4xx/5xx; commit-failure handling could leave a dangling transaction and hide the root cause. Fixed. 14 Medium Email.Office365 Attachments returned still transfer-encoded and keyed by content type (crash on two attachments of one type). Fixed. 15 Medium CI/CD Write-scoped tokens with persisted credentials, actions pinned to mutable tags, tag name interpolated into shell, NuGet publish without tests and with failures swallowed, unpinned pip installs. Fixed: least-privilege permissions, SHA pins + Dependabot, env-var passing, tests before publish, --skip-duplicate, pinned mkdocs-material. 16 Medium Payments (Tpay, Adyen) Webhook verification does not match the vendor protocol (Tpay: form + md5sum + JWS; Adyen: HMAC over colon-separated fields in additionalData). Fails closed, so not exploitable, but non-functional. Fixed in 2.0: Tpay verifies md5sum and X-JWS-Signature (chain to the Tpay root), Adyen the HMAC from additionalData.hmacSignature.

docs.title: Payments
docs.text:
• New TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Security.WebhookSignature (constant-time FixedTimeEquals, FixedTimeEqualsIgnoreCase, IsSecretConfigured) and PaymentIdentifier (IsSafe, EnsureSafe).
  • PaymentWebhookRequest.Headers/Query are case-insensitive regardless of the dictionary assigned; TransactionStatusChangePayload.QueryParameters is never null.
  • All providers: fail-closed on empty secret/signature, constant-time comparison, PaymentUniqueId populated from the payload, Processing events returned as Ignore, identifiers validated before URL interpolation, JsonDocument disposed.
  • CashBill: legacy path verifies the MD5 signature; error messages no longer contain the expected value; missing secret -> "Signature verification is not configured.".
  • Revolut: v1.{timestamp}.{body}, WebhookToleranceSeconds (default 300), rotation signatures.
  • Przelewy24: documented sign field sets with unescaped-unicode JSON; currency normalised once.
  • PayU: SHA-1 supported, unknown algorithms rejected. PayNow: stable Idempotency-Key, EXPIRED.
  • Stripe: missing WebhookSecret/header -> Fail; async payment events handled with ids.
  • Adyen: missing success treated as failure; merchantReference/pspReference in results.
  • HotPay: the signed service name is the one sent.

docs.title: ExceptionHandling
docs.text:
• DefaultExceptionHandlingProvider: validation -> 400; everything else -> 500 with "An unexpected error occurred."; constructor overloads (), (IHostEnvironment), (bool).
  • Middleware uses GetRequiredService, skips writing when the response has started, clamps the status code to 400-599. ExceptionOccuredResult honours the model's code. Duplicate DI registration removed. Docs and agent prompt rewritten against the real API.

docs.title: WebApi
docs.text: • HttpClientSettings.RetryUnsafeHttpMethods (default false) -> Retry.DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods().

docs.title: MediatR
docs.text:
• ICachePolicy.GetCacheKey -> {Type.FullName}:{SHA-256(JSON)} via CacheKeyGenerator.
  • LoggingBehavior no longer serializes the request; stack trace no longer concatenated into the message template. CachingBehavior uses structured log templates.

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
• TokenReplacingMailMessageBuilder: single-pass regex replacement, HTML-encoded {{token}}, raw {{{token}}}, HtmlEncodeVariables option, null-safe arguments.
  • DefaultMessageBuilder: single-pass, longest-key-first, HTML-encoded by default ((bool) ctor).
  • SmtpEmailProvider: one recipient only (FormatException on lists), CatchAll required when IsProd = false, EnableSsl defaults to true, proper Message-ID.
  • Office365EmailProvider: attachments decoded and keyed by file name.

docs.title: MediatR.ML
docs.text:
• ImageClassificationOptions.TrainingRoot, ModelsRoot, MaxImageBytes (default 10 MB).
  • TrainImageClassificationModelCommandHandler confines both paths (ArgumentException outside the roots, InvalidOperationException when roots are not configured).
  • ClassifyImageCommandHandler validates presence, size and JPEG/PNG signature. JPEG detection accepts any FF D8 FF header.

docs.title: EntityFramework / Querying
docs.text:
• QuerySortingExtensions: sort field must be a plain identifier; ApplySorting(..., allowedSortFields) overloads; Dynamic LINQ parse errors rethrown as ArgumentException without type details.
  • PagingQuery<T>: MaxPageSize (default 1000, static + per-instance), Page >= 1, 1 <= Count <= max, overflow-safe skip.
  • TransactionFilterAttribute: rollback on 4xx/5xx results; AggregateException when both commit and rollback fail. UnitOfWork: commit/rollback release the transaction in finally.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
• All workflows: permissions: contents: read by default, persist-credentials: false, actions pinned to commit SHAs (with version comments), .github/dependabot.yml for github-actions.
  • ci.yml: build/test job separated from the gh-pages deploy job (only the latter has contents: write).
  • release.yml: dotnet test before publishing, every package pushed from artifacts/package/release with --skip-duplicate, the job fails when any push fails, environment: nuget (add required reviewers in repository settings). Publishing uses nuget.org Trusted Publishing: the job exchanges a GitHub OIDC token for an API key valid for one hour, so no long-lived NuGet key is stored in the repository.
  • release-notes.yml: tag name passed through env, not interpolated into the script.
  • bump-deps.yml: full test run before the PR is created.

docs.title: Action items for the repository owner
docs.text:
1. Rotate the CashBill secret for the shop named in the removed test data, in the CashBill merchant panel. The value has been in git history since commit ed838d6; rotation is the only reliable remedy. If the repository is or was public, also purge the history (git filter-repo) and force-push, which is a destructive operation that was deliberately not performed here.
  2. The sandbox CashBill secret in tests/TailoredApps.Shared.Payments.Tests/appsettings.json is a test-environment credential; move it to user-secrets/CI secrets if the sandbox shop matters.
  3. In repository settings, add required reviewers to the new nuget environment so tag pushes cannot publish packages without approval, and make the Docs guard and Build & Test PR checks required on master. Create the nuget.org Trusted Publishing policy and the NUGET_USER secret described under Releasing in Contributing, then delete the old NUGET_API_KEY secret and revoke that key on nuget.org.
  4. Configure ImageClassification:TrainingRoot / ModelsRoot in hosts that use the training command, and pass allowedSortFields to ApplySorting for endpoints listing sensitive entities.
  5. Review consumers that relied on the old behaviours: 400 with exception message (now 500 generic), raw HTML in e-mail variables (now encoded; use {{{token}}}), SMTP without TLS (EnableSsl now true), multi-recipient strings in SendMail, POST retries via the WebApi resilience defaults.

docs.title: Follow-ups (not done in this change)
docs.text:
• Tpay and Adyen: notification verification now follows the vendor protocols, but it has not been exercised with a real sandbox notification - make a test payment before going live. Adyen: the Hosted Checkout session and reading its outcome follow the API specification, also without a test in the Adyen environment.
  • A failing gateway is no longer reported as PaymentStatusEnum.Rejected: the HTTP providers throw PaymentGatewayException (2.0), and from 3.0 Stripe does too (before: StripeException).
  • CachingBehavior no longer returns default for a cache miss on a value-type response (fixed in 1.5.1: a default value is treated as a miss and the handler runs). In 2.0 the problem is gone: CachingBehavior uses HybridCache, which tells a miss from a cached default value and protects against the handler running concurrently for the same key.
  • Amount conversion to minor units truncates and assumes two decimals; add a shared ISO-4217 helper.
  • PayU order creation shares one pooled handler that does not follow redirects (fixed in 1.5.1; it used to create a handler per order). It still bypasses the named client. OAuth tokens (PayU, Tpay) are fetched on every call.
  • EF: session-level SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL is SQL-Server-only and redundant; multiple AddUnitOfWork registrations cross-wire contexts; audit collector skips proxied entities; HasDefaultValue(DateTime.UtcNow) bakes a constant into migrations.
  • Package hygiene: Nullable off in most projects, no PackageReadmeFile in most packages, floating x.* versions without a lock file, SourceRevisionId from UtcNow, dead TFM conditions.
  • PagedAndSortedRequest duplicates PagedAndSortedQuery; add [Range] attributes.
